title: stab480 v9 respec: optimizer hot-loop pace defect (k3 fire) - NS-on-GPU streaming, in-process commit read, grad-memmap persistence
body:
## Why (wall receipt — the k3 fire was a design defect, not instability)

The v8 stabilize leg (refs #480) was k3-killed at 2026-07-09T21:47Z: ≥54 min without banking a block whose v6 baseline is 11.7–13.5 min (79.7–83.0 s/step), GPU duty cycle 3.1% mean, trainer CPU-busy at ~178% of one core. Three live stack samples (leg-close receipt, refs #480) caught the optimizer step crawling through three CPU-bound phases. No NaN, no divergence, no CUDA error: the v7 commit-starvation cure (file-backed optimizer state) and the k3 pace requirement are in direct tension in the v8 design. This issue owns the v9 respec; no relaunch happens before this spec is frozen and implemented.

Class extraction (bottleneck ledger, refs #207): a memory-wall cure that relocates a hot-loop working set to slower storage must carry a pace receipt at the same rung — commit ceilings and step ceilings are ONE budget, not two.

## The three receipted defects

1. **Muon Newton–Schulz on disk-paged memory (dominant).** The inner optimizer's `_zeropower_via_newtonschulz5` executes on CPU over file-backed memmapped shadow parameters. For grown-width tensors (16384×32768) the NS matmul chain over paged memory converts an ~80 s step into a multi-thousand-second one.
2. **Commit-governor subprocess in the hot loop.** `_read_commit_gb` shells out to PowerShell (seconds per call). A live stack caught it firing INSIDE the step path — consistent with defect 3 re-arming the governed lazy-create branch every step.
3. **Front-load/zero_grad teardown race.** `zero_grad(set_to_none=True)` propagates to the inner optimizer whose params ARE the shadow params, tearing down the front-loaded `.grad.f32` memmap references each step — so step()'s lazy-create branch (and its per-parameter governor assert, defect 2) re-fires for every parameter on every step.

## Spec floor (v9 requirements; deviations need a dated comment here)

- R1: NS orthogonalization never runs over disk-paged memmaps. Either (a) stream each matmul-active shadow tensor to GPU for its NS chain (the GPU is idle during opt.step; VRAM cost is one tensor at a time, well inside the k1 band), or (b) keep the matmul-active (grown-width) tensors heap-resident, memmap residency retained for pure elementwise state (exp_avg / exp_avg_sq / momentum). Choice (a) preferred — it preserves the v8 commit profile (~47 GB, 46 GB under the v7 failure point).
- R2: the commit read becomes an in-process API call (Windows memory-status API via ctypes; microseconds). Governor semantics — phase-boundary asserts, ≥6 GB free-commit floor, abort-not-degrade — unchanged.
- R3: `.grad.f32` references persist across steps: zero_grad must zero-in-place or re-attach the persistent memmap, never tear down to None. The lazy-create branch may fire at most once per parameter per process lifetime; a receipt counter proves it (field `grad_lazy_creates`, must equal 0 after front-load).
- R4: in-run pace gate — the k3 enforcement moves inside the runner: if the first block since (re)launch has not banked within 2× the v6 baseline (≤27 min), the runner checkpoints what is consistent and aborts cleanly with a PACE_GATE marker. A coordinator-observed stall is the fallback, never the mechanism.
- R5: relaunch resumes from block-04 step-806 (unchanged, hash-verified); kill conditions k1/k2/k3 + CUBLAS-twice carry over verbatim; the existing prediction registers on refs #480 remain graded-as-closed for the v8 leg — the v9 leg gets a FRESH register filed before launch (register law: never retrofit).

## Acceptance

- AC1: implementation PR cites this issue (refs only), CPU-only unit evidence that R2/R3 hold (governor call count per step = 0 in steady state; grad_lazy_creates = 0).
- AC2: a pace smoke — one governed block on the real checkpoint — banks in ≤27 min with s/step receipted, VRAM inside k1, commit ≤ 58 GB.
- AC3: queue row added to refs #591 by dated comment; dispatch order after the services-restore row.

The corpus census (2026-07-09) adds the sharpest fact: **no owned training holding has EVER been scanned against the frozen suite hashes** — the predicate (refs #440) interlock in the freeze spec has never executed.

Ground truth read this session from `docs/spec/eval-suite-freeze-v1.md` (Status: Frozen, effective 2026-07-08): 7 datasets pinned with test-split sha256 (MMLU-Pro 12032 rows `5fdd1b75…`, GSM8K 1319 `fb581f02…`, MATH-500 500 `200806fb…`, ARC-Challenge 1172 `c0e7635e…`, HumanEval+ 164 `4e8dbe98…`, MBPP 500 `88d69020…`, HellaSwag 10003 `6a78734f…`); GPQA-diamond PIN-PENDING on a license-consent gate; spec clause: the predicate "must verify training data against these hashes BEFORE any capability claim cites this suite." The spec doc is frozen — what is MISSING is the executed declaration + quarantine + scan. That is this issue.

## Deliverables (one PR + receipts)

1. **Freeze-declaration receipt** (`receipts/` per the freeze doc's schema, extended):

A dataset pinned later joins a future suite VERSION; it is never appended to a frozen one. This retires the "queued for when the operator is next active" wait entirely.

Receipt fields: `contamination_recheck` (must be 0 to unblock; a nonzero finding is reported unspun, never cured silently), scan-code sha, corpus manifest shas, `scan_ts`.
4. **Post-freeze held-out addition**: ONE never-before-run held-out eval selected by a PUBLISHED mechanical rule (deterministic function of `eval_freeze_hash` over a named public candidate pool; rule text lands in the PR). No discretionary pick.

## Acceptance criteria

Worktree-only (never checkout/switch in the main tree); PR body refs-only (refs #123 #591 #440 #582 #585); no personal names, no absolute local paths anywhere; NEVER --no-verify, hook-skip, or tree-shaping to pass a gate — a gate block = stop and report verbatim; no GPU use (CPU/scripting only); receipts are serializer-emitted JSON, never hand-assembled; report claims carry their measurement command + raw output tail.

Sprint objective (window through 2026-07-12): every GPU window executes back-to-back from FROZEN preregs — zero design latency between a window opening and a governed leg launching. - A leg dispatches ONLY if its prereg pointer is frozen (kill conditions + receipt schema registered on the owning issue) and its admissibility preconditions are receipted.

title: optimizer-state param-id conflation: global model-state ordering used as muon-local slot keys (3 sites, shared-module fix + retro-audit)
body:
## Defect class

Optimizer-state param-id convention conflation: GLOBAL model-state-dict ordering (185 names) used as keys into MUON-LOCAL-keyed optimizer state dicts (140 entries, keys 0–139, `split_param_groups` muon-only construction order). The two numberings diverge as soon as any AdamW-routed param (embed/norm/head) interposes in the global ordering — reads pull from the wrong slot, writes clobber unrelated slots.

Found via the #480 leg-1 run-v4 fail-closed abort → #577 investigation (ground truth: real model constructed on CPU, `split_param_groups` called directly). Receipts on #577 (comments 4928038121, 4928061344 + the ruling-delta comment).

## Known affected sites (three, one shared)

1. **Write side**: `cbase_grow_rung2_stabilize.py:424-434` (`build_transplanted_resume_checkpoint`) — global `param_names.index(key)` written into muon-local `muon_state`. Effect measured: 74 shape mismatches in the staged bundle (60 FF misfiled across all 20 layers + 25 attention slots clobbered). Being cured in the #480 lane's own script (input-side keying remap; shared module untouched).
2. **Read side (SHARED module)**: `resolve_gate_momentum_buffer` — `p5_ratio_audit/run_p5_audit.py:1257`, called by `transplant_muon_ff_momentum`. Docstring says the convention was "verified against a real checkpoint's optimizer.pt" (#466) — plausibly true for the pre-split single-optimizer format, stale since the file-backed split-optimizer landed (commit 2445c4b, 2026-07-08).
3. **Truncation checker**: `_enumerate_missing_optimizer_state_ids` — probes global ids against the muon-local dict, so it reports "missing" for entries filed under a different key. Its false positives generated the `disclosed_deviation` narrative in the staged manifest and the earlier `N_LAYERS_VERIFIED_MOMENTUM=15` hybrid ruling. Measured refutation: all 60 FF source momentum buffers present and nonzero (rms 2e-5–2e-3, depth-smooth).

## Fix spec (frozen)

- ONE authoritative mapping helper: construct-model → `split_param_groups` → bidirectional `name ↔ muon_local_id` map (plus `name ↔ global_id` for the model dict), exported from the module that owns `split_param_groups`; all three sites consume it. No site computes `.index()` against a state-dict key list again.
- AC1: property test constructing the real model on CPU (no GPU), asserting round-trip name↔id identity for all 140 muon entries and that every FF tensor's momentum slot resolves to a shape-matching buffer.
- AC2: the truncation checker re-implemented on the helper; run against the seed checkpoint must report 0 missing (the measured ground truth).
- AC3 (retro-audit, line-item): every receipt/ruling whose derivation consumed outputs of sites 2 or 3 gets re-derived under fixed indexing — at minimum: the `N_LAYERS_VERIFIED_MOMENTUM=15` ruling, `receipts/cbase-grow-rung2-stabilize-transplant-wall-diagnostic-20260709T130000Z.json`, and `receipts/p513-p3-forensic-20260709T041108Z.json` ("silently-zeroed momentum" — potentially the read-side artifact). None of their conclusions is overturned without receipts; each gets a dated confirm-or-correct note.
- No in-place mutation of historical receipts; corrections land as dated sibling notes (custody discipline).

Refs #577 #480 #466. Builder: cheap-agent executable against this spec; the retro-audit notes route through coordinator gate.

title: grow boundary: saved optimizer bundle carries pre-grow shapes - load policy must satisfy the momentum-provenance register constraint
body:
Filed from the #480 leg-1 RUN v4 receipt (2026-07-09T16:52Z, /tmp/stab480-run-leg1-v4.log): the streaming fail-closed restore assert caught `shape mismatch idx=4 backbone_model.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj.weight key=momentum_buffer: dst=(32768,1024) src=(16384,1024)` at PRE_LOAD_OPTIMIZERS_STATE. Severity note: torch's stock `Optimizer.load_state_dict` does NOT shape-check state values — without the fail-closed override this mismatch loads silently and corrupts (or crashes) at the first step. Deaths v1-v3 of this leg (ArrayMemoryError, silent, commit-exhaustion in the load cast) were all masking this defect. The commit-exhaustion class is separately CURED (v4 markers: peak 75GB through the phase that killed v3 at 93.66GB).

## Decision structure (coordinator rules on the lane's investigation receipts)

Facts owed by the running investigation (stab480):
- F1 mismatch enumeration: saved-vs-live shape for every bundle entry; prediction = exactly the 45 transplanted ids mismatch.
- F2 bundle provenance: did the BUILD write a grown/transplanted optimizer bundle anywhere (transplant-ckpt tree, staged-save pieces) while run_v0_segment reads the SOURCE checkpoint's bundle path (wiring defect), or was no grown bundle ever produced (production defect)?

Constraint that binds the ruling (register, not convenience): the #449 rung-3 prereg matched protocol requires a momentum-provenance-verified snapshot; the stabilize leg's optimizer-state provenance is measurement-relevant for the c/d_comm observables. Any load policy adopted here must be receipted (which bundle, which transform, verified how) so the provenance chain survives into the rung-2 measurement receipts.

Any transform of saved state (e.g. twin-duplication of momentum rows per the frozen scale convention) is applied by an auditable step with its own receipt (source sha, transform, output sha), never in-place on the checkpoint.
- AC4: relaunch under the adopted policy with two-point attestation; the leg's per-block receipts declare the optimizer-state provenance (bundle path + policy id).

title: watchdog tail-poll mega-burst on cockpit relaunch (~2^16 identical lines from one kill-receipt row)
body:
## What's happening

The operator cockpit's `state/activity-ledger.jsonl` shows two mega-bursts, each landing in
a single second, each dumping roughly 2^16 (65,536) near-identical lines into the activity
feed — the actual flood the operator saw, and something #571 (banner/input/status regions +
render clip) and #574 (P0-B: receipts/board watermark+exclusion+coalescing) do NOT fix, since
both bursts are entirely on the tail-poll path (`pollTail` over `restartLogPath` /
`killReceiptsPath` in `services/activity-feed.ts`), a separate mechanism from the receipts/board
watcher path those two PRs gate.

## Evidence

**Trigger correlation — exact, 2-for-2.** Both bursts land 1-2 seconds after a
`"target":"cockpit"` relaunch event in `liveness-watchdog-restart-log.jsonl`. None of the five
`"target":"server"` relaunches in the same ~15h window correlate with any burst.

| Cockpit relaunch (`ts`) | deadPid → relaunchPid | Burst (`ts`) | Burst size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-09T08:22:07.3555346Z | 36128 → 34836 | 2026-07-09T08:22:08 | 65,913 lines |
| 2026-07-09T05:08:07.2574640Z | 44028 → 7044  | 2026-07-09T05:08:09 | 65,779 lines |

This is structural: the activity-feed engine is mounted inside the cockpit process itself
(`useEffect(() => startActivityFeed(), [])` in `screens/repl.ts:703`), so a cockpit relaunch is
a fresh boot of the very thing hosting this engine.

**The anomaly is one specific row, not "everything replays".** Within the first burst, 65,028
of the 65,913 lines are the byte-identical text `"server killed by watchdog (reason
unavailable)"` — the only text `formatWatchdogLine` can produce for a row shaped
`{pids: [...]}` with no `reason` field. The resolved `llama-server-kill-receipts.jsonl` has
exactly 3 lines total (confirmed unique via `sort -u`), and exactly ONE of them matches that
shape. Its mtime (Jul 8 16:27) predates both bursts by many hours — the source file was never
rewritten, so this isn't file growth.

Meanwhile `liveness-watchdog-restart-log.jsonl` (859 lines, all confirmed unique via `sort -u`,
each with its own `ts` roughly 30s apart) is NOT proportionally exploded — its ledger counts
(44-748 depending on marker owner) are consistent with real, individually-tailed watchdog
events accumulated over hours, not a replay artifact. Whatever mechanism is at fault treats
the two tail-polled files very differently despite sharing the same `setInterval` tick.

**Magnitude — the 2^16 lead.** 65,913 and 65,779 both sit within 0.6% of 65,536 (2^16); the
identical-line count 65,028 is in the same band. This is unlikely to be coincidence and points
at a 64KB buffer size, a uint16 wrap, or a byte-offset-consumed-as-a-repeat-count confusion
somewhere in the boot-time tail path (candidates: `freshTailState`'s initial byte offset being
read/treated as an iteration count by some consumer; a fixed 65536-byte read/loop bound that a
tiny 873-byte file's read loop increments incorrectly — e.g. by a constant instead of by the
actual bytes read — running the full 65536-count regardless of the file's real size). The
asymmetry between the two files would follow naturally if the bug scales with a FIXED buffer
size rather than the file's own byte length: the kill-receipts file's short content lets many
more "iterations" of a broken loop complete audibly within the same wall-clock window than the
larger, slower-to-process restart-log content does.

**Ruled out:** file rewrite/growth (kill-receipts mtime predates both bursts); a naive
"whole-engine-restarts-repeatedly-in-a-tight-loop" theory replaying BOTH files symmetrically
(would require restart-log's diverse content to explode by the same factor, which it does not).

**Natural experiment (cliswap72's manual cockpit kill/relaunch, 2026-07-09 ~16:53:29Z,
post-#574 build):** watched `state/activity-ledger.jsonl` live through it. Result: **a burst
DID fire, but only half the pattern reproduced, which discriminates the two files' mechanisms
cleanly.**

- **Restart-log half: confirmed, reproduces on manual boot.** A clean burst of exactly 859
  lines landed at `16:53:29Z` — an exact match to `liveness-watchdog-restart-log.jsonl`'s
  CURRENT total line count at that moment. The per-owner counts (748 `remeasure466`, 60
  `b3fix513`, 44 `growevent466`, plus the various one-off relaunch lines) match the SAME
  distribution seen in the original two mega-bursts' restart-log contribution. Critically,
  `liveness-watchdog-state.json`'s `cockpit.deaths` array was UNCHANGED (still shows only
  `2026-07-09T08:22:07Z`, the original incident) — the watchdog itself never recorded this
  manual kill as a death/relaunch event, yet the full file still replayed. This confirms: **any
  fresh cockpit process boot — watchdog-triggered or manual — causes exactly one full replay of
  the CURRENT restart-log content**, because `restartTail`/`killTail` are process-local
  (`let`-declared inside `startActivityFeed`, reset via `freshTailState()` on every call) with
  no persistence across a process boundary. This is a real, deterministic, always-happening
  defect whose severity scales with how large `restart-log` has grown by the time of the next
  boot (currently 859 lines; will keep growing).
- **Kill-receipts half: did NOT reproduce on this manual boot.** Zero `"(reason unavailable)"`
  lines appeared anywhere in this burst window (`grep -c` = 0), even though the same static
  3-line kill-receipts file (containing the one `{pids:[...]}`, no-`reason` row) was in scope
  the whole time. This means the ~65,000x explosion is NOT simply "fresh boot replays
  kill-receipts once" (that alone would produce 3 lines, not 65,000) — it requires an
  ADDITIONAL condition present during the two historical WATCHDOG-triggered relaunches but
  absent from this manual one. Leading candidate: something specific to the watchdog's own
  automatic relaunch sequence (its own retry/wait logic around `resolveKillReceiptsPath` or the
  `watchdogStatePath` read, possibly racing a concurrent rewrite of that state file during an
  automatic relaunch, which a manual kill+relaunch by an operator doesn't exercise the same way).

Net: the restart-log full-replay-on-boot mechanism is now CONFIRMED and reproducible at will
(any cockpit restart). The kill-receipts 65,000x explosion remains open — it needs either a
watchdog-triggered relaunch to observe live, or the instrumentation counters below to catch it
retroactively next time it fires.

## Impact

The operator's cockpit can see a near-identical mega-flood again on the next
server-kill/planned-outage cycle that also restarts the cockpit process, even with both #571
and #574 merged — the dominant flood driver by volume (94.8% of the historical ledger) is not
yet fixed.

## Fix shape (companion PR in progress)

1. **Containment (ships regardless of root cause):** a per-tick emission cap on the tail-poll
   path, mirroring #574's burst-coalescing philosophy for receipts — if a single `pollTail`
   invocation would emit more than a small threshold of lines in one tick, render ONE
   "N watchdog events collapsed (tail-poll anomaly)" summary line instead of N individual ones,
   plus a diagnostic note to a debug log so the anomaly stays visible for root-cause work.
2. **Instrumentation (for root-cause):** invocation counters/logging on
   `pollTail`/`freshTailState`/`startActivityFeed`, active ahead of the next real cockpit
   relaunch, to directly observe the call/byte-offset pattern rather than infer it from ledger
   output after the fact.

title: Spec lattice: full-tree audit receipt (196 docs), the ember-cli coverage gap, and the spec-consumer wiring rule
body:
## Audit receipt (2026-07-09, operator question: do full spec sets exist / are there dead docs?)

Method: 6-leg workflow — 5 strict classify legs (per-doc: last-commit date, content read, whole-tree citation grep; instructed to prefer STALE-SUSPECT when torn) + 1 adversarial verify leg re-deriving every dead/stale verdict (a suspect stays condemned only with a NAMED successor or contradiction; default REFUTED). Universe: all 196 tracked .md excluding fixtures/receipts.

**Distribution:** 122 CURRENT / 51 STALE-SUSPECT / 12 HISTORICAL / 8 DEAD-CANDIDATE / 3 TEMPLATE-DATA at classify; after adversarial verify of all 59 dead+stale suspects: **0 CONFIRMED-DEAD, 2 CONFIRMED-STALE, 54 refuted back to CURRENT, 3 reclassified HISTORICAL.**

Answer to the operator's dead-docs question, with receipts: the doc tree is substantially alive — date-based staleness suspicion overwhelmingly failed citation checks. Exactly two demonstrably rotten docs:

1. `docs/research/drafts/nc2-recipe-stack-draft.md` — superseded by `docs/research/nc2-recipe-stack-2026-06-10.md` (same issue #28, same scope, status DRAFT).
2. `tools/ember-cli/specs/services-prompt-suggestion.md` — spec text still says the service does not exist while the feature SHIPPED (`src/services/prompt-suggestion.ts` + test, PR #199). A spec lagging shipped reality is the worse failure mode of the two.

## The real findings (what the audit actually surfaced)

1. **Coverage is asymmetric, not rotten.** Research/governance is spec-rich: heavily-cited binding contracts (INVARIANT 57 cites, nc2-own-technique 52, deviations 30), 13 frozen preregs, a deviation protocol. ember-cli — the operator's primary touch surface — has FOUR spec docs total for its entire codebase, and one of the four is the stale one above. The body is the least-specced organ and the most operator-visible one.
2. **No lattice structure exists.** Docs are a pile with an index, not a graph: no parent/child links, no spec-to-consumer map, no per-node statement of what enforces it. A spec constrains builders only through a consumer (gate, probe, test, CI, spawn-prompt quote) — an unconsumed spec is documentation, not constraint.
3. **Freshness wiring exists but skips the body:** the docs-freshness checker + daily pass covers README-described surfaces; `tools/ember-cli/specs/` is outside its reach — which is exactly where the one lagging spec sat.

## Mechanism (just-in-time, no documentation program)

- **Cure the 2 confirmed-stale now** (lane dispatched with this issue): supersession header on the draft pointing at its successor; status correction on the prompt-suggestion spec (SHIPPED, PR #199).
- **Body spec floor:** any PR adding a new ember-cli component or feature carries its spec node (create or update under `tools/ember-cli/specs/`) — merge-gate checklist item. First instances: the render-integrity + resident-colleague builds (#561/#565) land their specs with their PRs.
- **Spec-consumer wiring rule:** a spec node claims CURRENT only if it names its consumer (the gate/test/probe/loop that reads it). The audit JSON is the seed index; nodes with no consumer get one named or get reclassified HISTORICAL at the next freshness pass.
- **Freshness loop extension:** docs-freshness checker scope grows to include `tools/ember-cli/specs/`.

Side-by-side on the operator's screen: an agent-CLI window (right) where he types, converses, and watches the agent actively reason/plan/work/call tools — versus ember-cli (left), where he 'cant type in, dont even know where', 'cant talk/converse/understand whatever the fuck is happening', and 'do not see ember actively reasoning, planning, working, researching, or doing anything.'

His framing test, binding: **imagine being the model resident in ember-cli, with the operator forced to communicate with you there.** Today that communication is impossible. The gap is not rendering polish — it is that ember-cli is a mute dashboard when the constitution says it is where ember **lives, acts, speaks, and is audited** (P-C), with **bidirectional conversation through the body** (GOAL §7).

## What this makes primary

The transcript + input box are the SPINE of ember-cli. The observatory/board is a pane, not the product. The field exemplar is the agent-CLI class the operator uses daily: persistent bottom input, conversational turn history, streamed replies, visible between-turn activity.

## Acceptance criteria (experience-level, each needs a live receipt — unit-green does not count, per the #242 posture)

- **A. INPUT ALWAYS (P0 — rides #561 P0-A):** a visibly anchored input affordance at the bottom of the window from the moment it opens (visible cursor + placeholder text), focus-safe, and keystrokes land even while the feed is busy. The operator must never not-know where to type. Banner locked top, input locked bottom, regardless of content scroll (his prior directive, restated).
- **B. CONVERSATION SPINE:** typing + Enter renders an operator turn; the resident model's reply STREAMS as an ember turn via the served backend. The turn history is the main region and scrolls independently of the locked chrome. This works TODAY with the resident model — no new capability is a precondition for the surface.
- **C. VISIBLE WORK:** between turns, ember's real activity renders as legible, edge-triggered items (runs starting/finishing, receipts landing summarized — #561 P0-B is the floor, never raw-path spam), plus the current goal-mode objective + current step (from the #211 organ state) always visible. Fed ONLY by real process/receipt state: a keyframed or invented activity item is a fabricated receipt in visual form (P-C law).
- **D. REASONING VISIBILITY:** while the resident is generating or a goal-mode step is executing, the window shows a live working state (streaming tokens / step label / spinner) — never a frozen or silent screen. 'Quiet forge' mode is a one-line status, never absence.
- **E. EXPERIENCE GATE:** side-by-side capture against the field exemplar at the operator's real half-screen viewport + live-resize probe; blind test: a stranger can tell 'this is an agent I can talk to and watch work.' Predicted operator score >= 8 with the side-by-side receipt before any delivered ping.

## Honest scope

This issue binds the SURFACE and its wiring to real state. The depth of autonomous reasoning it displays is the C6/C7/#211 ladder and grows on its own receipts — but the surface must render whatever exists NOW (board runs, training legs, server activity, goal state) legibly, and the conversation must work NOW with the resident model. A perfect surface over a mute organism would show an honest 'idle'; today the organism is active and the surface shows nothing — that inversion is the defect.

title: The body owns its liveness: absorb watchdog functions into ember-cli, retire the external daemon to an OS-native restart rule
body:
Operator architecture question, 2026-07-09: why would a perfected body need an external watchdog at all? Is it part of ember-cli? Does the body stop working without it and never recover? The question is the design truth — this issue is the retirement path.

## Current state (honest)

An external hand-rolled PowerShell daemon (liveness-watchdog.ps1) polls the cockpit process, the model server, and planned-outage markers, and relaunches the dead. It did real work overnight (cockpit restarted twice, server restarted twice after an outage window overran — restart-log receipts). It is also itself fragile: today's deploy crashlooped four instances in seven minutes (13:52–13:59Z), flashing visible console windows on the operator's screen — the checker needed a checker. Scaffolding without a retirement path becomes the building.

## The decomposition (three needs, three different answers)

1. **The body's ORGANS die (model server).** The body must own this natively: spawn, health-poll, restart-with-backoff, circuit-break — inside ember-cli. #556's parent-liveness tether landed the first half (server dies with its parent); the restore half (CLI resurrects a dead server) must move from the watchdog into the CLI.
2. **The body crashes from its own defects.** Not a supervision need — a defect class. Render/feed errors must be contained, never process-fatal (#561 is the current instance).
3. **The body's own process dies** (kill, OOM, power). The only genuinely irreducible external need — a process cannot resurrect itself. The answer is a boring OS-native restart rule (Task Scheduler restart-on-failure or an equivalent 5-line supervisor), not a stateful polling daemon.

## Ladder

- r1: server supervision absorbed into ember-cli (restart-with-backoff + circuit breaker; planned-outage marker semantics move into the CLI/server contract).
- r2: crash-free bar — CLI survives its own render/feed exceptions with an in-pane error event, receipted.
- r3: external supervision reduced to one OS-native restart-on-failure registration for the CLI process itself.
- r4: liveness-watchdog.ps1 deleted from the process table permanently; restart-log lineage archived.

## Acceptance

- Kill the model server → CLI restores it natively, event rendered, receipt written.
- Kill the CLI process → OS rule restores it, receipt written on next boot.
- Zero hand-rolled watchdog processes running; window enumeration clean.

Constitution anchors: P-C (body co-equal, never lags the organism), §7 ladder (ember self-operates, audited), and the dependence-ratchet direction — external crutches must shrink measurably.

body:
Frozen spec from the evidence-bar calibration register (#123 comment 4925052695, tick 28). These are the three cheapest rejection-risk shields in the paper map (pure scripting, zero GPU) plus the freeze-declaration mechanics they feed. They implement register factors Q6 (data/L3), Q7 (compute), and A1 (hygiene).

## Component A — eval-contamination scan (Q6b, feeds A1)

`scripts/paper/contamination_scan.py`, CPU-only, deterministic, **model-free by construction** (n-gram + MinHash only — no embedding model anywhere, so no L3 debate can even start):

- Inputs: (1) an eval-suite manifest (JSON list of eval files; the frozen suite when A-D lands, any suite path meanwhile), (2) corpus shard paths/globs.
- Method: 13-gram exact-collision rate per eval item against every shard (normalized whitespace/case), plus MinHash-Jaccard near-dup score (128 perms, shingle=13).
- Output receipt: `receipts/paper/contamination-scan-<UTCts>.json` — per-item {item_id, max_13gram_collision, max_minhash_jaccard, worst_shard}, suite-level summary, thresholds echoed.
- Pre-registered thresholds (in-receipt, not tuned post hoc): collision>0 on any 13-gram window of length >=3 consecutive grams OR jaccard>=0.5 → item flagged CONTAMINATED-CANDIDATE; flagged items are QUARANTINED from claim-bearing evals and listed in the receipt — never silently dropped.
- AC: runs end-to-end on the current corpus + any 10-item toy suite fixture; unit test with a planted duplicate (positive control) and a clean item (negative control); receipt json.loads-validates; no network.

## Component B — corpus provenance manifest emitter (Q6a)

`scripts/paper/provenance_manifest.py`:

- Per corpus shard: {shard_path, sha256, source (URL/identifier or UNKNOWN), fetch_date (or UNKNOWN), transform_chain: [{step, script, input_sha, output_sha}], model_in_loop: false attestation field}.
- Machine-checkable: where transform inputs still exist on disk, the emitter RECOMPUTES the chain hashes and marks each link VERIFIED/UNVERIFIABLE.
- Honesty rail: missing provenance = explicit UNKNOWN rows, never omitted shards. The manifest's own summary counts {verified, unverifiable, unknown} — the paper cites those counts as-is.
- Output: `receipts/paper/provenance-manifest-<UTCts>.json` + AC: covers every shard the training configs reference; unit test with a synthetic 2-shard fixture (one verifiable, one UNKNOWN).

## Component C — per-run compute ledger emit (Q7)

Runner-level hook (same insertion class as the #544 <ROOT> substitution — receipt-write time):

- Every training-run receipt gains a `compute_ledger` block: {tokens_seen, optimizer_steps, wall_seconds, sec_per_step_mean, tflops_est (formula stated in-field), peak_vram_gib (incl. memmap/offload accounting), watts_series_ref (if #118 instrumentation present, else null)}.
- Backfill utility for EXISTING claim-bearing receipts: fills fields derivable from present data, UNKNOWN otherwise — never estimates silently.
- AC: next runner invocation emits the block; backfill run on the rung-2 receipt set produces a table checked into `receipts/paper/compute-ledger-backfill-<UTCts>.json`; unit test on a fixture receipt.

## Component D — freeze-declaration mechanics (A1; coordinator-gated, BLOCKED-BY benchmark mandate completion)

Not builder work yet — tracked here so A1 has a home: when the benchmark-mandate suite completes, the coordinator declares the freeze as {commit_hash, suite_manifest_sha256, ts} in a receipt; every pre-freeze number is classified into a labeled development appendix; ONE never-before-run held-out eval is then selected by a published mechanical rule (script in this repo, seeded by the freeze commit hash — no human pick). Builders do not implement D until the freeze declaration lands.

## Rails

CPU only; no GPU; no model inference anywhere in A/B; never touch training code paths beyond the C receipt-write hook; hooks ON (never --no-verify, never alter tree state to pass a gate); redaction law applies to every new receipt (run scripts/redact_for_landing.py + both-root-family byte-grep); PR refs-only (refs #123 #487 #118 #544 — no closing keywords); worktree isolation.

body:
## Constitutional-derivation gap (standing jun-sim wince since 2026-07-08 — converting to a spec)

GOAL.md SS5: "Ember owns its full vertical... The ladder runs continuously; which layer comes home next is earned by receipts on where borrowed code costs most." C4 gates completion on it. Nothing measures it: docs/ember-owned-substrate-diagnostic.md is a static map with no trend, no receipt-per-window, no answer to "is the borrowed bill shrinking?"

## Spec (measurement first, then the lens consumes it)

A nativization-motion receipt, regenerable by script, per window or per landing:
1. Enumerate the vertical's layers (inference engine, training substrate/autograd, optimizer, GPU kernels, math) per the diagnostic map.
2. Per layer, two measured columns: (a) BORROWED-WEIGHT — external-package import count + LOC of ember code that calls it (mechanical grep, receipted); (b) CRITICAL-PATH SHARE — does the creation path (current rung's training/growth run) transit it (yes/no, from the run's import manifest).
3. MOTION metric: delta vs the previous receipt — a layer coming home shows borrowed-weight falling to 0 with the run still passing; flat across N windows = the drive is stalled (SS5 says it "starts now", so flat is a finding, not neutral).
4. Board hook: the receipt is board-consumable so a future C4-adjacent row can gate on "motion receipt exists and is fresh", not self-report.

## AC
- AC1: script emits the receipt from a clean tree with zero manual input; runs in seconds (grep/AST-level, no GPU).
- AC2: receipt carries per-layer numbers + deltas + the diagnostic-map version it read.
- AC3: first receipt lands with the PR (baseline), second receipt after any subsequent landing proves the delta machinery.

title: liveness-watchdog: main-tree freshness leg — operator screen must auto-follow remote master post-merge
body:
## Gap (jun-sim tick 2026-07-09, delivery-surface catch)

The cockpit renders from the MAIN tree; landings merge to REMOTE master via worktree PRs. Nothing pulls the main tree afterward. Receipt: main tree sat 7 commits behind (6ee4167 vs 31a316d) with the operator's board showing pre-merge reality (8G board while master had 9G), until a coordinator hand-pulled. Also: the fs-watcher re-rendered stale June receipts as fresh events when git touched old files during fetch — staleness produces noise, not just lag.

## Cure

Extend tools/ember-cli/liveness-watchdog.ps1 with a freshness leg (or a dedicated puller it supervises):
- Poll public/master every ~2 min (git fetch + rev-list HEAD..public/master --count in the main tree).
- Behind AND clean (no tracked modifications, no untracked collisions with incoming paths) -> git pull --ff-only, then render an activity event: "tree advanced to <sha> (<n> commits)".
- Behind AND dirty/colliding -> render a LOUD activity event naming the residue files (the operator sees staleness as an event, never as silent old pixels). Never stash/delete on its own.
- Precedent: the WEB-CAD master-autofwd daemon (30s poll, ff-only, SKIP-if-dirty, responsibility for dirty cleanup stays with the actor that dirtied).

## AC
- AC1: merge a docs PR remotely; within 2 poll cycles the main tree is at the new sha and the activity ledger carries the advance event — zero human action.
- AC2: with a deliberately dirty tracked file, the leg SKIPS and renders the residue event instead; nothing is lost.
- AC3: kill-discipline untouched — the leg never kills anything; repo-guard untouched.

title: redaction utility: tracked, pin-aware, enumerated-fields-only (hard-fail on hash-pinned bytes)
body:
## Why (receipts)

Four functional artifacts were corrupted by ad-hoc landing-time redaction in ONE day (2026-07-09): the surface-2 probe default (#533, cured #536), the tracked tokenizer (#531/#534, non-loadable), receipt-internal citations (#535, cited_missing=24 rename drift), and hash-pinned evidence bytes rewritten at landing (#537 — frozen-rows twin sha broke a pinned chain; embedded Python regexes corrupted by backslash rewrites; a public HF URL mangled). The #537 law is ruled: **a file whose sha256 is pinned by any other receipt lands byte-exact or does not land**; redaction operates on enumerated path-valued fields only, never blanket regex over file bytes. Today the "utility" is an untracked ad-hoc script re-sent to each landing lane — the 5th corruption is prevented by a tracked tool, not vigilance.

## Deliverable

`scripts/redact_for_landing.py` — tracked, self-testing, the ONLY sanctioned redaction path for landing lanes.

## Frozen AC

- **AC1 — explicit file list only.** Positional args are files; directories and globs are REFUSED (exit 2 with message). No recursive mode exists.
- **AC2 — pin scan, hard fail, no override.** Before touching anything, build a pin index: scan all tracked `receipts/**/*.json` + `scripts/ember_totality/receipts-*/**/*.json` for 64-hex sha256 values. For each input file, sha256 its current bytes; if that hash appears in the pin index, REFUSE to modify that file (exit 3, print the pinning receipt path(s)). There is NO flag that overrides this.
- **AC3 — enumerated fields only (JSON).** For `.json` inputs: rewrite ONLY string values reachable at key names in the in-script manifest of path-valued fields (e.g. `path`, `*_path`, `cache_source`, `fork_dir`, `receipt`, `png`, `capture_path`, `cmdline`, `script`) — recursive descent by key name, values only. Whole-file byte regex is structurally absent for JSON inputs. Non-JSON inputs: refused unless the extension is in a small doc allowlist (`.md`), where term replacement runs line-wise.
- **AC4 — word-boundary terms.** The term list is applied with word boundaries; the self-test includes an English-word-noise case (a term that is a substring of an ordinary word must NOT match).
- **AC5 — corruption-class regression tests.** Self-test (`scripts/test_redact_for_landing.py`) covers at minimum: (1) pinned-file refusal with pinning-receipt named; (2) enumerated-field rewrite leaves sibling non-enumerated fields byte-identical; (3) an embedded Python regex string containing backslashes in a NON-enumerated field survives byte-exact (the #529/#537 corruption class); (4) a public URL in a non-enumerated field survives byte-exact; (5) word-boundary non-match; (6) idempotence (running twice = running once).
- **AC6 — no behavior change anywhere else.** No existing file modified except adding the two new scripts; existing tests still pass (`python -m pytest scripts/test_524_m4_momentum_transplant.py scripts/test_p5_513_resolver_fix.py -q` or the repo's standard quick set).

## Rails

CPU-only. The utility itself must never be run against tracked receipts as part of this PR (tests use fixtures in a temp dir). PR from a lane-owned worktree cut from public/master; refs #525 #529 #531 #533 #535 #537 — refs only.

title: fix: C2 regression — landing redaction rewrote bytes inside hash-pinned evidence; restore byte-exact + hash-pin law
body:
## Finding (REVIEW tick, 2026-07-09 — C2 regression root-caused)

C2 flipped GREEN→RED between board runs 065411Z and 081147Z. Root cause: the landing redaction **rewrote bytes inside hash-pinned evidence**. The tracked `receipts/ember-d3-native-loop/d3-gym-fresh-rows-offset20-len12-20260708T221652Z.json` no longer matches the sha256 its candidate receipt pins (disk `7c9361aa…` vs pinned `9acd3496…`), so the C2 probe's clause-(D) hash check correctly rejects the candidate. (The probe's RED reason hid this: its failure list caps at `failures[:3]` and the three June candidates fill it — display defect, secondary.)

The redaction damage inside the three files landed by the C2 cure PR:
- a **public HuggingFace URL** mangled: `https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/rows?…` → `httplocal:rows?…`
- **embedded evaluation-script code corrupted**: backslash→slash rewrites inside Python string escapes and regexes (`\s*` class patterns broken), i.e. the redaction's path-normalization regex ran over embedded CODE, not just path fields
- repo-root absolute paths rewritten repo-relative (the sanctioned rule — but applied to a hash-pinned file)

Due diligence executed this audit (receipts in the cure PR): word-boundary founder-name scan + coordination-tree path scan + user-dir scan over all three pre-redaction originals = **zero hits**. The apparent name-substring counts are English-word substrings in external dataset text — the same substring-matching defect class that corrupted the tokenizer (#531 comment).

## Law (coordinator ruling, board-color-bearing)

**A file whose sha256 is pinned by any other receipt lands byte-exact or does not land.** Redaction and hash-pinning are structurally incompatible on the same file: if a pinned file genuinely contained a leak, the path is quarantine + documented-absent or a disclosed provenance-transition re-pin — never a silent byte-rewrite that breaks the chain. Additionally: redaction utilities operate on **enumerated path-valued fields only**, never blanket regex over file bytes (embedded code, URLs, and external data are off-limits).

## Frozen AC (restore lane)

1. Replace the three tracked files under `receipts/ember-d3-native-loop/` (`d3-gym-fresh-rows-offset20-len12-20260708T221652Z.json`, `d3-native-loop-20260708T221708Z.json`, `d3-broader-multifamily-fresh-rows-reconstructed.json`) with their byte-exact pre-redaction originals (coordinator supplies the bytes from off-tree custody copies).
2. PR body pastes: sha256 of each restored file; the frozen-rows sha MUST equal the candidate-pinned `9acd34969911…`; and the zero-hit leak-scan disclosure. The PR body never references off-tree custody paths.
3. Rationale framing: the redacted twins never validly landed as evidence — their hash pins fail by construction — so restoration makes the original landing honest; this is not a post-hoc edit of valid evidence. This issue is the disclosure record.
4. Expected board effect: C2 returns GREEN with `git-anchor: ANCHORED` on the next totality run; state it in the PR body.
5. Secondary (separate commit, same PR): `test_c2.py`'s reason string discloses truncation — `-> {failures[:3]}` becomes `-> first 3 of {len(failures)}: {failures[:3]}`. No other probe logic changes.

## Redaction-utility half (rides the landmine thread)

The landing utility must (a) refuse to rewrite any file whose sha256 appears anywhere else in the tree (pin scan before rewrite), and (b) restrict replacements to enumerated path-valued JSON fields. One comment referencing this instance goes to #525/#502.

title: feat: frozen-tokenizer reconstruction script + serve preflight (serving-tokenizer custody mechanization)
body:
## Gap (mechanism-gap sweep, 2026-07-09)

Serving identity (#508) now depends on a byte-exact reconstruction of the frozen training tokenizer (sha256 `2c557e7f…`, oracle = `receipts/tokenizer-freeze-20260611T154111Z.json`), which exists only as an **untracked, gitignored file** under `models/cbase-serving/`. No standing mechanism protects it: a models-dir cleanup deletes it silently, and regenerating it currently requires re-deriving the method from a lane transcript. The tracked `tokenizer/tokenizer.json` is a redacted edition that does not load (#531 comment) — by design it stays that way.

## Frozen AC

1. **Commit the reconstruction as a script**: `scripts/tokenizer/reconstruct_frozen_tokenizer.py`. Inputs: the tracked redacted edition + the freeze receipt (oracle sha). Method (proven 2026-07-09): duplicate-preserving raw parse (object_pairs_hook), base_size=245 (8 specials + 237 byte-alphabet), merge-rank walk computing `true_string[id] = true_string[id_a] + true_string[id_b]` with component-id resolution filtered to `id < current_id`, residual ambiguity resolved by sha256-oracle search over the (small) combination space, targeted byte-span replacement so nothing else in the file changes. Output: the reconstructed file under `models/cbase-serving/` (gitignored — NEVER tracked) + an ids-only receipt.
2. **Purity gate (hard)**: the script contains NO name literals — it is purely constructive (derives strings from merges structure). CI-safe check in the PR: grep the script against the repo redaction term list = zero hits; the script never prints derived strings (ids and shas only).
3. **Serve preflight**: the serving path asserts sha256(tokenizer file) == the freeze-receipt sha before binding; on absence, runs the reconstruction script and re-verifies the oracle; on mismatch, fails closed with the sha pair in the error. No silent fallback to the tracked edition (it cannot load anyway).
4. **Receipt**: each regeneration writes an ids-only reconstruction receipt (counts, gap ids, oracle shas, combination index) — no vocab strings.
5. Unit test: script runs against the tracked edition in CI-safe mode (structure walk + ambiguity enumeration WITHOUT writing output) and asserts the expected duplicate-key/gap-id fingerprint, so drift in the tracked edition is caught.

## Rails

The tracked `tokenizer/tokenizer.json` is read-only input — never modified, never staged. Reconstructed output and receipts carry vocab ids only, never strings. PR stop-at-open, refs-only.

title: custody: re-verify every sha-pinned in-tree artifact named by a receipt (freeze-artifact integrity probe)
body:
Receipt-class gap, proven today: the 58ddf8d consolidation scrub byte-replaced name literals INSIDE tokenizer/tokenizer.json on 2026-06-28, silently corrupting the frozen training tokenizer (3 vocab-id collisions via duplicate scrubbed keys, merges referencing out-of-vocab tokens, unloadable by tokenizers 0.22.2, sha 6923a523... vs the freeze receipt's pinned 2c557e7f...). Nothing detected it for 11 days; the first consumer to notice was today's serving launch crash (refs #508). The shard receipt's provenance_230 row honestly re-pinned the premise but the LOADABILITY and receipt-vs-disk sha agreement were never re-checked by any standing loop.

## AC
1. The custody checker (or a new board-condition probe) enumerates receipt fields matching *_sha256 that name an in-tree file, and re-verifies: file exists AND sha matches the pin. Mismatch = custody violation row with the receipt path + field + expected/actual sha.
2. Provenance-transition rows (old->new re-pins like provenance_230) suppress the mismatch ONLY when the new sha verifies — a re-pin to a hash that itself fails on disk is still a violation.
3. Format-validity spot-probe for known loadable artifact classes (tokenizer.json -> tokenizers load; *.pt header read) on the pinned files, fail = violation.
4. First run's findings land as a receipt; today's tokenizer case must appear in it (or be explicitly annotated as cured by then).

Small sonnet lane; extends the existing custody sidecar machinery.

title: ember-cli: activity must render as transcript blocks in the conversation, not statusline ticker lines (operator category correction, second receipt)
body:
## The correction (operator, 2026-07-09, verbatim class)

> All i saw was just... literal, activity lines with timestamps at the bottom of the statusline/input box, which is just... stupid.

This is the SECOND receipt of the same category miss (first: 2026-07-07 — "activity" was implemented as a status feed when the operator's word denotes *the organism working live like an agentic session*). The prior fix shipped activity as timestamped lines pinned near the statusline/input box. That is a status feed again. The category: **completed activity belongs IN the conversation transcript as first-class blocks, at its temporal position, scrolling with history.**

## The exemplar (the operator pointed at a Claude Code session's history)

The reference transcript anatomy, from the exemplar he quoted:

```
  Ran 5 shell commands

[assistant reply text...]

✻ Running scheduled task (Jul 8 9:59pm)

● Stop Task
Task: produce the end-to-end receipt that ember-cl... · stopped

● Agent(GH App runtime receipt (retry lane)) Haiku 4.5

● Write(state\spec-drafts\rung2-stabilize-config-respec-v1.md)
Wrote 70 lines to state\spec-drafts\rung2-stabilize-config-respec-v1.md
# Rung-2 stabilize: config re-spec v1 (frozen)
... (content preview)
… +64 lines

● 2 background agents launched (↓ to manage)
@stab480
@topo516

● Running 1 shell command…
```

Anatomy: (a) tool-run summary blocks ("Ran 5 shell commands") interleaved with chat text; (b) named tool cards with object + result size + content preview + fold marker ("+64 lines"); (c) agent-spawn cards with label + model class; (d) background-launch cards with the lane names; (e) scheduled-task markers with timestamps; (f) ONLY the currently-running action lives at the bottom ("Running 1 shell command…").

## Contract (acceptance)

1. Every organism action — tool run, file write, lane/agent spawn, tick fire, training-run launch, receipt bank, run completion — renders as a **block in the conversation scrollback** at its temporal position, visually distinct from chat text, persisted in the session transcript (scrolls away like any message; reload-safe).
2. Block anatomy per the exemplar: one-line summary (verb + object + count/size), expandable/folded detail (first N lines + "+K lines"), class tag where applicable (model tier, lane name, run id).
3. The bottom statusline area keeps ONLY the live in-flight line (current action + spinner). Completed activity NEVER appears only there. The existing ticker lines are removed or demoted to the live-line role.
4. Experience gate before any delivered claim: side-by-side capture of ember-cli vs the exemplar transcript at the half-screen primary viewport + live-resize reflow probe; a fresh reader must identify tool-runs / spawns / writes in ember's transcript as fast as in the exemplar; score-prediction >= 8 against the exemplar, receipt attached.
5. Semantics receipt in the PR body: this issue's operator quote + the statement of the category ("activity" = agentic-session transcript, not status feed) so the third recurrence is structurally impossible to ship in ignorance.

title: totality runner must refuse or loudly stamp a stale/dirty run tree (board ran 7 commits behind master, silently)
body:
## Incident (2026-07-09)

A post-merge board re-run executed in a main tree 7 commits behind public/master (HEAD 1cbd1fb vs master 6675e2a). The #497 C-CUSTODY cure was absent from the code that ran, so the receipt reproduced the pre-cure verdict (cited_missing=23, documented_absent=0) and the run was discarded after coordinator forensics. Nothing in the runner or receipt surfaced the staleness (receipt printed pinned=None, no tree-vs-remote check).

## Mechanism gap

"Board re-renders on the new master after every merge" silently assumed the run tree tracks master. All landings are worktree+PR-shaped, so nothing ever fast-forwards the main tree; every post-merge board run is stale by default until someone syncs by hand.

## Fix (spec floor)

1. Runner startup resolves the run tree HEAD and the canonical remote master SHA (git ls-remote; offline fallback = recorded FETCH_HEAD with a named degraded mode). Record both in the receipt: run_tree_sha, remote_master_sha, tree_is_stale, behind_by.
2. Default on staleness: REFUSE with a one-line sync instruction. An --allow-stale-tree opt-out exists for archaeology runs and stamps tree_is_stale=true into the receipt AND the rendered board line, so a stale receipt can never read as board truth silently.
3. Dirty-tracked-file check, same treatment (tree_dirty list in receipt; refuse by default). Untracked run outputs exempt.
4. The README renderer refuses a receipt carrying tree_is_stale/tree_dirty unless the same opt-out is passed.
5. Tests: fixture repo behind its remote -> refusal, and stamped receipt under opt-out; dirty tracked file -> same.

## Acceptance

A board run from a stale or dirty tree cannot produce a publishable receipt without a visible stale/dirty stamp in both receipt JSON and rendered board.

title: Serve the ember-created cbase 2.2B behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (external-benchmark test-subject leg)
body:
## Why

The external-benchmark mandate evaluates the EMBER-CREATED artifact (cbase 2.2B rung-2 lineage, b1-snapshot) as the test subject; harnesses (lm_eval et al.) speak OpenAI-compatible HTTP. No such endpoint exists in-repo — all current inference is in-process `.generate()` (density_ab_bench.py). Scout receipt: standard LlamaForCausalLM architecture, no custom layers; direct transformers serving is viable (Route A).

## Spec floor

- `scripts/serve_cbase_openai.py` (~150-line FastAPI shim, port 8083 default):
  - Checkpoint: `models/cbase-grow-rung/rung2-event-grow-rung2-20260708-real/b1-snapshot/model.pt`, SHA256-validated against its manifest BEFORE load.
  - **Config inferred from state_dict tensor shapes** — never hardcoded from the seed config (the checkpoint is post-grow; intermediate_size differs from the seed 4096). Startup log + `/health` report the inferred dims.
  - Frozen training tokenizer (path + existence receipted).
  - `/v1/models`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` (naive last-message routing), greedy default, `max_tokens` honored, `usage` token counts populated.
  - `--device cuda|cpu`, requests serialized behind a lock (single GPU stream).
- **One-model-at-a-time rule in the docstring and a startup guard**: refuse `--device cuda` if `:8082` (27B reference server) answers `/health` — the benchmark scheduler owns the swap window.
- Tests (CPU-only, no GPU in CI/dev): state_dict key-match vs the inferred-config model, 1-token CPU generate smoke, endpoint schema tests via TestClient.

## Out of scope

GGUF conversion (lossy — would taint subject fidelity), vLLM, batching, benchmark runs themselves.

## Acceptance

CPU test suite green + a receipted GPU smoke (one completion) in the first serialized window when :8082 is down.

title: ember-cli native GitHub identity: App-token client + gh tools (credential-agnostic build; App install is a separate leg)

## Why (operator mandate, 2026-07-09)

ember/ember-cli must own its GitHub capability the way its maintainer tooling does — without it, every GitHub action routes through the coordinator, which contradicts the operation ladder (GOAL §7) and the dependence direction (#479). title: repo hygiene law: growth is not progress — retention rules, consolidation cadence, size-vs-progress metric, first cleanup pass
body:
Operator, 2026-07-08, confirmed as law: **repo size/growth ≠ ember completion/progress, and repo size/growth ≠ elite research repository quality.** Tonight's measured accretion, no cleanup rule anywhere: 2,272 tracked files; 205 docs; 601 scripts; 939 tracked receipts + 1,637 more untracked on disk; 156 open issues; stale tmp packs in .git. Every mechanism this program builds ADDS files; nothing ever removes one. Elite research repos are lean: every file load-bearing and current, deletion a first-class operation (git history is the archive).

**The rules (land in GOVERNANCE.md as one short section via this PR chain):**
1. **Docs:** every doc under docs/ declares what supersedes/invalidates it (the GOAL §8 map pattern, generalized). A superseded doc is DELETED in the superseding PR — never left beside its replacement. Version-suffixed spec files (v1, v2) may keep at most the live version + the frozen prereg editions the claims cite.
2. **Receipts retention:** receipts cited by the board, the credibility battery, an open claim, or a frozen prereg are PROTECTED. Uncited receipts older than 30 days move to the annex pattern (custody model already supports annex_attested) in one quarterly sweep PR; the working receipts/ set stays readable end-to-end by a stranger.
3. **Scripts:** a script referenced by no playbook, board probe, test, or doc is dead — each hygiene pass proposes its deletion with the reference-scan as evidence.
4. **Issues:** consolidation cadence — issues silent >14d get one disposition comment: folded into a carrier issue (pointer), parked-with-path in the floor contract, or surfaced for operator kill (L7: kill stays operator-only; consolidation with a pointer is not a kill).
5. **The metric (receipts, not vibes):** the totality board run appends a working-set line — tracked files, docs count, scripts count, tracked receipts, open issues — to the board receipt. The SIM/review watches the TREND against battery-grade movement: working-set growth across a window where no battery row improved = a named wince. Growth must buy graded evidence or it is clutter.
6. **Issue creation discipline (binds the coordinator too):** extend an existing carrier issue over opening a new one whenever the work shares a track — six new issues in one night is itself a data point this law exists to correct.

**First cleanup pass (lane-executed, evidence-per-file, deletions via reviewed PR — nothing auto-deleted):** reference-scan docs/ and scripts/ for unreferenced/superseded candidates; propose the deletion manifest with per-file evidence (what referenced it last, when, superseded-by); triage the 1,637 untracked receipts into cited/annex/delete; prune .git tmp packs. Acceptance: the manifest PR lands with GOVERNANCE rules + the board working-set line, and the follow-up deletion PR shrinks the working set while every battery grade holds or improves.

4. title: Commit-exhaustion crash class: Windows commit limit (16GB fixed-init pagefile) unifies all 2026-07-08 native crashes + clean MemoryErrors; cures = file-backed optimizer state + commit-aware preflights
body:
Measured receipt (Win32_OperatingSystem + Win32_PageFileUsage, 15:3xZ): physical 63.6GB; pagefile fixed-init 16GB (max 32GB), peak usage today 13.4/16GB; commit limit 79.6GB; commit USED 60.6GB while physical-in-use was only ~31GB; commit AVAILABLE 19.0GB at the same instant 'free physical' read 31GB.

**Unified mechanism for the day's entire crash record:**
- Clean ArrayMemoryErrors (13GB corpus concat at two free-RAM levels; 2GiB recheck; 512MiB per-shard read at '28.7GB free') = allocators that check commit charge upfront and fail honestly. Free-physical was never the binding metric; commit-available was.
- Native crashes (widen ACCESS_VIOLATION x3 under the contended window; clone() SIGSEGV at cpu_offload_adamw.py:106 on the first-ever offloaded opt.step()) = reserve-then-commit-on-touch paths: reservation succeeds, first touch cannot be committed, access violation instead of a clean exception. CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 + healthy post-crash GPU/RAM on the clone crash rule out async-CUDA and leak mechanisms.
- The quiet-window widen success (the #446 discriminator) = lower commit charge, exactly as this mechanism predicts. #446's machine-state closure stands; this issue names the machine state precisely.
- Why the memmap cures worked: file-backed pages charge NO commit. The 'every bulk read becomes memmap' posture (#455) was the right cure adopted under a wrong label (fragmentation).
- The clone() trigger quantified: first opt.step() of the offloaded 2.2B config initializes ~26GB of fresh CPU-side state (fp32 shadow + exp_avg + exp_avg_sq) against a 19GB commit-available ceiling.

**Cures (engineering-first, no system-settings dependency):**
1. cpu_offload_adamw.py: optimizer state becomes FILE-BACKED (np.memmap-backed torch tensors, mode r+, sha-keyed under scratch/) — eliminates the commit ask AND makes optimizer state checkpointable (feeds the rung-3 momentum-transplant decision on the d_comm prereg). Lane on it.
2. Commit-aware preflight everywhere a launch gate exists: assert commit_available > planned_new_commit + margin; receipt carries BOTH commit-available and free-physical. Free-physical alone is banned as a launch gate (the governor's current ram.free_ram_gib check reads the wrong counter for this class).
3. Optional box-level lever, operator-owned, NOT blocking either cure: the 16GB fixed-init pagefile is undersized for a 63.6GB heavy-commit ML box; system-managed or larger init would raise the ceiling. The engineering cures above stand alone without it.

Acceptance: (a) file-backed optimizer state lands with a test proving zero large commit delta across opt.step() first execution; (b) probe + governor preflights print commit numbers; (c) one full instrumented probe step completes at rung-2 scale (the #429 merge-bar receipt). refs #429 #446 #455

title: PREREG: rung-2 d_comm prediction — per-class, per-convention, frozen before the rung-2 grow event
body:
Pre-registered BEFORE any rung-2 grow executes (rung-2 machinery in flight on #429; this freeze must precede the real grow event or the result is post-hoc). Supersedes the retracted #327 interpretation (see the correction comment there); derivations panel-verified (2 independent seats + arithmetic-verify leg with code-read receipts).

## The observable
d_comm per #327's definition, measured with the #448 decomposition fields (step_rms_post, pushforward_step_rms, cos_alignment) — MANDATORY; a rung-2 d_comm without the fields does not test this prereg.

## Frozen inputs (derivation chain in the tick-18 note)
- q is exact and distribution-independent per class: q_gate = q_up = 1; q_down = 0.5 under exact duplication. Under the #280 antisymmetric-perturbation operator, q_down acquires an O(eps) correction (parameterization arrives with the #280 implementation PR); q_gate/up unchanged. Every receipt pins the operator version.
- r by LR convention, dimension-invariant across a strict doubling (max dim doubles; 16384>1024 holds at rung-2): flat-LR r = 1/sqrt(2) all classes; repo scale-convention (scale=max(1,m/n)^0.5, code-confirmed in run_p5_audit.py:1899-1932) r_gate/up = 1.0, r_down = 1/sqrt(2).
- OPEN INPUT to pin before measurement: which convention the PRODUCTION training loop's Muon applies (the audit harness uses the scale convention; the production loop must be code-read and quoted — builder item below).

## Predictions (gate-only, comparable to rung-1; per-class values in the tick-18 note)
Under the scale convention, gate-only independence null = sqrt(2) = 1.41421. Rung-1 measured 1.13526 implies c = +0.356 (flat-LR: null sqrt(1.5)=1.22474, c = +0.149).

Bands, frozen now:
- (i) ALIGNMENT REPRODUCES: rung-2 gate-only c in [0.25, 0.45] (scale convention, decomposed via #448 fields) — partial commutation is real, stable, and function-preservation-predicted; the law becomes d_comm(geometry, c) with c the physics term. Claim-ladder: promote to L2-candidate (measured cross-rung regularity).
- (ii) ALIGNMENT VANISHES: |c| < 0.05 — rung-1's c was a reconstruction artifact (its pre-grow checkpoint was inverse-net2net-derived, no optimizer state); the independence null stands for genuine snapshots. Claim: measurement-hygiene finding, D4.
- (iii) OTHERWISE — attribution via the decomposed r vs q vs c (which input broke names the follow-up; no post-hoc band invention).

## Measurement conditions (all mandatory)
1. GENUINE pre-grow snapshot saved WITH optimizer state immediately before the rung-2 grow (rung-1's reconstruction confound must not recur — this is actionable now because rung-2 has not grown).
2. Layer 0, gate_proj primary (rung-1 comparability) + per-class breakout (gate/up/down separately — down carries the only q≠1 term and is the sharpest semantics check).
3. #448 fields emitted; optimizer-state provenance recorded; operator version/sha pinned; LR convention of the applied update quoted from the code that ran.
4. Measurement occurs before any post-grow training beyond the rung-1 protocol.

## Decision clause (what this changes)
If band (i): momentum TRANSPLANT (pushforward optimizer state through the widen map) is predicted to beat momentum reset on post-grow loss-spike recovery; rung-3's grow procedure adopts whichever a paired A/B receipt supports. If band (ii): reset stands, no transplant machinery is built. The observable buys a procedure decision, not bookkeeping.

- Pin the production Muon LR convention (code-read + quote; NOT the audit harness).
- Low-rank-matched MC null (EXP-C1b spectra) — secondary to c-attribution.
- Full-text novelty pass over the adjacent literature (2605.15435, 2605.13405, 2604.04281, 2406.02469, 2305.02869) before any public claim beyond this repo.

title: Corpus defect: massive late-region near-duplication in shards-v0 (shard-19 x1044 concentration + tail zero-clean) — repair-vs-certify decision tree
body:
## Corpus defect: late-region massive near-duplication in shards-v0 (two independent receipts) — repair-vs-certify decision tree

**Evidence (both landed 2026-07-08, independent lanes, independent instruments):**
1. **Shard-19 concentration** (`w1c-knee-sweep-20260708T112944Z.json`, histogram run): the fwd_1m pool's 16 needle windows match ~1,044 corpus positions EACH (per-row counts dead flat, 1013–1083) and **100% of all 16,472 matches lie in one shard, v0-00019.bin** — zero in the other 25. The needle positions themselves sit inside shard 19's window range: the shard contains ≥89-token spans repeated ~1,044×.
2. **Tail zero-clean** (P1 decontam builder run, exit log banked by the sweep lane): in default tail-mode (held_out_window_start 6,814,292 ≈ shard v0-00025.bin), **0 of 192 candidate windows were clean at W=13** across 6 rounds — every candidate's windows appear elsewhere in the corpus. (The banked W1 control batch at pool-start 2^22 ≈ shard 16 found 16/16 clean in round 1 — that region is fine.)

**What survives:** the W1 control receipt (its 16 windows verified clean under the strict any-match convention — internal corpus repetition does not invalidate a clean-region batch). **What is now suspect:** (a) effective corpus size — if whole shards are near-duplicate content, every capability-per-token and per-corpus-pass claim carries an inflated denominator; (b) the 10/10 DIRTY region verdicts from the W1c scout (`w1c-scout-master-20260708T080858Z.json`) — those scans predate per-shard histograms; their match masses (10.8M mid_corpus, 53.6M back_1m) may ALSO concentrate in the duplicated shard set, in which case the "corpus-wide contamination" read collapses into a small excisable shard set.

**In flight:** decode probe (prose-duplication vs degenerate-filler at matched positions in shard 19 + a shard-25 tail sample) + shard-19 internal structure (contiguous vs scattered), assigned to the scan lane.

**Decision tree (pre-registered now, before the probe lands):**
- Decode = degenerate filler (whitespace/format blocks) → corpus-assembly defect; cure = **dedup/excise → shards-v1 manifest** with a receipted diff (window counts before/after, sha chain), then re-run the 10-region scout against v1 with per-shard histograms; K-batch certification returns as plain binary absence against v1.
- Decode = real prose repeated ~1,044× → document-duplication defect; same cure path but the dedup is document-level (harder); interim: certification predicate = absence outside the quarantined shard set (already receipted clean for fwd_1m at W=13).
- Per-shard histogram re-run on 2–3 heavy regions (mid_corpus, back_1m, back_50k) decides whether the scout's DIRTY verdicts are shard-concentrated: ≥90% of matches in ≤3 shards → excision certifies everything; diffuse → true corpus-wide duplication and the frequency-accounting predicate (#374 thread) returns from the archive.

**Constraint carried:** corpus manifest sha (aa48f6ee…) is pinned by existing receipts — v0 is never edited in place; any repair lands as a NEW manifest (shards-v1) with lineage, and existing receipts keep citing v0 truthfully.

Refs: #372 (scan harness arc), #374 (cert re-spec thread — frequency framing now conditionally superseded), #118 (P1 sweep — tail finding source), #435 (decontam regen).

title: VOID receipts record truncated 16-hex sha prefixes in supersedes[] — void_supersession requires full 64-char digests

Found during the C(-1) annex extension (PR #426): the grow-op-rung2-void receipt's supersedes entries carry 16-hex-char sha256 PREFIXES; void_supersession.py matches on (basename, full-64-char sha256), so the supersession never fired for the fabricated pair and they needed separate annex attestation. The lane computed both full hashes and confirmed they start with exactly the recorded prefixes — truncation, not mismatch.

**Cure options (either, with fixtures):** (1) void_supersession accepts an unambiguous hex PREFIX >= 16 chars (must match exactly one file; ambiguity = no match, fail-closed); (2) convention doc + writer check: future VOID receipts record full digests (the existing receipt is append-only history and stays as-is either way — option 1 is the only one that retro-covers it). PR stop-at-open, no close-keywords.

title: repo-guard branch-name check + GitHub rename API footgun: renaming a branch with an open PR auto-closes the PR (2 occurrences 2026-07-08)
body:
Twice on 2026-07-08 (06:33Z and ~06:5xZ, two different lanes) the same trap fired: a lane hits repo-guard's <type>/<slug> branch-name check on a PRE-EXISTING non-conforming branch, reaches for the GitHub branch-rename API, and the rename DELETES the old ref and AUTO-CLOSES the open PR instead of migrating it (headRefName never changes). Both lanes recovered (recreate ref at same sha + gh pr reopen), but the recovery is manual and the trap is silent.

**Cures, either/both:** (1) repo-guard exempts branches that already have an open PR (check is advisory for pre-existing branches, binding for new ones); (2) document in GOVERNANCE.md: never rename a branch with an open PR via the raw API — commit in detached HEAD (repo-guard allowlists HEAD) and push to the existing ref, as finisher lanes now do. Note: master has no GitHub branch protection, so the CI branch-name failure is cosmetic today — if that changes, this becomes a hard wall. PR stop-at-open, no close-keywords.

title: Cockpit process death is invisible: frozen pixels pass for a live body (liveness gap)
body:
Found during the build-1059671 swap census: the operator's cockpit pane had been a CORPSE for up to ~11h — the cockpit binary had exited, only the `cmd /k` wrapper kept the pane open, and the last-rendered frame (board summary included) sat frozen at the operator's screen position looking exactly like a live cockpit. Nothing detected it: the board kept updating on disk, the receipts stayed fresh, and every green condition was invisible at the only surface that matters (P-C: the body IS the audit channel — a dead body showing a fresh-looking frame is a fabricated receipt in visual form, per the constitution's own words).

The staleness badge (#392/#404) does not cure this class: a dead process freezes the badge too — a frozen 'board: 2m ago' looks fresh forever.

**Acceptance (two halves):**
1. IN-APP: the cockpit renders a visible liveness signal that decays WITHOUT re-render — the cheapest honest form is a wall-clock (HH:MM:SS, ticking every render cycle) in the header/status line: a frozen clock is visible death at one glance. A heartbeat FILE (cockpit writes ts+pid every cycle, e.g. state/cockpit-heartbeat.json) accompanies it so machine checks don't need pixels.\n2. EXTERNAL: a standing check (census tooling) compares pane-existence vs process-liveness vs heartbeat age and flags PANE-WITHOUT-PROCESS and HEARTBEAT-STALE as loud defects.

Rails: *_test.py suffix fixtures, PR stop-at-open, no close-keywords near issue numbers anywhere.

title: Shared _function_preservation_check() segfaults at rung-2 scale (memory lifecycle: two models resident, uncollected)
body:
Found during the C-BASE clause (d) dry-run rerun (PR #402 diagnosis lane).

**Defect:** `cbase_grow_live._function_preservation_check()` crashes with SIGSEGV (exit 139) deterministically when exercised at real rung-2 scale: the pre-grow (~1.19B param) and post-grow (~2.2B param) models are held resident simultaneously, uncollected, during the check. The helper was never previously exercised at this scale.

**Evidence (from the diagnosis lane, reproducible):**
- 6+ isolated hand-bisected repros; deterministic 2/2 crashes on the full script
- Fix confirmed 3/3 clean: release the pre-grow model before building the post-grow model
- The dry-run PR carries a local low-memory variant (same math, same imports of build_model/widen_state_dict, same PASS_TOL) with a module docstring explaining the divergence — the shared helper itself is intentionally unedited pending this issue
- Measured on the fixed path: fp_diff 5.72e-06 vs tolerance 1e-4 (PASS; rung-1 precedent 2.38e-6)

**Acceptance:**
1. The shared helper releases the pre-grow model (or otherwise bounds peak residency) before building the post-grow model; the fix must keep the check's math identical (same tolerance, same comparison set).
2. A regression test at a scale that reproduces the original crash shape (can be a reduced-but-representative residency test if full rung-2 scale is impractical in CI), named with the *_test.py suffix convention.
3. The dry-run's local variant is then retired in favor of the fixed shared helper (follow-up PR may do this).
4. PR stop-at-open; no close-keywords adjacent to issue numbers in title or commit headlines.

Repro script path: will be cited from the PR #402 branch once the diagnosis lane pushes (its report includes the isolated-repro script).

title: Board-time writers to canonical receipts/ round 2: milestone-reconciliation + publication-gate (the #387 sweep missed them)
body:
