title: cockpit: live window shows zero activity while the organism works; bottom UI region missized vs top

milestone.title: EMBER-03A: Visible live-graphs panel
milestone.description:
Predicted 2026-07-21. Forcing 2026-07-23. Minimal real loss and speed data plotted visibly in Ember CLI; no fixture-only acceptance.

Deliverable definition is immutable against deadline pressure; breach changes execution, efficiency levers, sequencing, or an operator-visible date/hardware decision, never scope or acceptance criteria.

body:
Two operator-observed defects on the LIVE cockpit window (2026-07-07, verbatim-class report):

1. **Zero activity in the window.** The cockpit displayed no activity during a period when the system was demonstrably working (merges landing on master, board run executing, research receipts being produced). The body is the operator's audit channel (GOAL P-C) — an organism that works while its body shows nothing is a P-C violation regardless of internal health. Expected: the window surfaces live signals (journal/receipt/run events) within seconds of them occurring; a quiet-but-alive state must still show liveness (heartbeat/last-event timestamp), never a static void.

2. **Bottom UI region missized/small compared to the top.** Layout defect in the live TUI: the lower portion of the interface renders undersized relative to the upper portion. Likely reflow/viewport-split bug (same family as the fixed-width findings in the live-resize probes). Needs: reproduction at the operator's real viewport (half-screen left split), a live-resize pass, and a fix gated on before/after captures.

Acceptance for closing: live demonstration receipts (#242 program bar — unit-green/self-report do not count): (a) a capture showing real-time event flow in the window while a background run produces receipts; (b) before/after captures at the operator viewport showing the bottom region correctly sized, surviving a live resize.

title: ember-cli: resize-back to a previously-seen size not detected (stdout.columns stuck at intermediate size)
body:
Split from #286 / PR #291 (disclosed residual, confirmed at gate from the committed captures). After the #291 fixes, the FIRST live resize reflows correctly (208x22 -> 105x55: clean full-width panel, pixel receipts in tools/ember-cli/state/captures-286/). But a SECOND resize back to a previously-seen size (105x55 -> 208x22) is not reliably detected: process.stdout.columns/rows remains stuck at the intermediate size even with an explicit _refreshSize() call, so the app renders a clean 105-wide layout inside a 208-wide window (capture: after-wide-again-208x22.png — left-half panel, right-half void).

Evidence from the #291 lane's isolation work: a minimal Bun+ConPTY repro OUTSIDE the app detects both resize directions correctly — the failure only manifests under the app's heavier repaint I/O, pointing at a Bun/ConPTY interaction (related background: oven-sh/bun#17803, columns/rows never auto-refresh on Windows) rather than a defect in the #291 provider/poller fix itself.

Severity: the operator's default workflow is live half-screen/full-screen resizing — a stuck-width layout in a wide window is a first-class visible defect, not cosmetic. Acceptance: ConPTY capture session with >=3 size transitions including a return to a previously-seen size; every transition reflows to full width within one poll interval; add the wide-tall-wide sequence to the capture battery as a standing regression check.

title: decontam mp scan: headroom assert scope + worker teardown on main-process death
body:
Incident receipt (2026-07-06 ~21:22-21:35Z, #193 persisting re-run attempt): the scan's main process died while its multiprocessing workers kept running — worker heartbeat rows continued appearing in scratch/w2-heldout-run/mp-progress-20260706T212233Z.jsonl for ~6+ minutes after the parent PID was gone, and the leaderless workers held ~20GB of system commit. That stranded commit then caused the NEXT launch attempt to fail the W2_DECONTAM_INSUFFICIENT_HEADROOM preflight (9.2GB free < 12GB required) — the leak from the first failure blocked its own retry. Cohort was reaped manually (kill receipts banked externally); free commit recovered 7.3GB -> 27.8GB.

Two defects, one fix each in scripts/w2_heldout/build_decontam_batch_mp.py:
1. ASSERT SCOPE: any headroom/commit assert that can fire after worker spawn converts a refusal into a leak. The assert must run PREFLIGHT (before Pool creation), and any mid-run resource check that trips must go through the same teardown path as normal exit, never a bare raise that kills the parent first.
2. WORKER TEARDOWN ON ANY EXIT: the parent needs a finally/atexit that terminates+joins the pool on every exit path (assert, exception, SIGINT). A worker that can outlive its parent is an orphan-commit bomb — this is the second commit-exhaustion incident of this class in 3 days (2026-07-04: leaked capture/probe processes, 5.8GB).

Acceptance: kill -9 the parent mid-scan in a test harness -> zero surviving workers within N seconds; assert-trip path -> zero surviving workers + nonzero exit + partial receipt written.

title: ember-cli welcome/status surface: 8 named layout+rendering defects vs field exemplar (fixed-width, border corruption, void dominance, status-bar artifacts)
body:
Operator-reported (2026-07-06, live screenshot of the running cockpit, wide-short viewport ~208x22): the welcome/status surface fails the field bar badly. Eight named defects from the pixels, each independently checkable in a ConPTY capture:

1. **Fixed-width layout in a wide window.** Welcome box occupies ~55% of columns; the input rule and status bar stop at ~40%; everything left-crammed with a dead right field. This is the same fixed-width class as the earlier live-resize failure — still unfixed at this viewport.
2. **Border/header corruption.** A stray `│` fragment renders beyond the welcome box's right edge; the box's own "ember" border label, a separate floating "▌ ember v0.0.0" header, and an orphaned "Tips for getting started" heading (top-right, with NO content beneath it) are three disconnected header fragments fighting for one identity.
3. **Void dominance.** One thin content strip at top; ~70% of the viewport is empty black below it.
4. **Status bar renders as ragged inverse patches.** Black-text-on-grey highlight runs (looks like accidentally-selected text, not design), and the first item is left-clipped (renders as "o observe").
5. **Unidentified grey filled bar** directly under the input line (~40% width) — reads as a scrollbar/progress artifact; no discernible function.
6. **Tip text truncated with "…"** at fixed width while half the window is empty.
7. **Empty-state is undesigned**: "Recent activity" / "No recent activity" / "/resume for more" as bare dim stacked lines with a stray horizontal rule.
8. **No token discipline**: a lone teal accent, a white heading, grey inverse blocks — vs the charmtone palette + glyph system already distilled in `tools/ember-cli/state/field-ux-map.md` §8b (which remains the binding taste doc).

Acceptance (all receipts, no self-report):
- ConPTY captures at BOTH operator viewports — wide-short ~208x22 AND tall half-screen ~105x55 — plus a live-resize probe between them (reflow required; clipped borders / dead columns / mid-word truncation = fail).
- Before/after rasterized frames side-by-side with the field exemplar's structure (single coherent header, content-sized bordered box, one clean muted status row, designed empty-state).
- Every defect above either cured in the capture or explicitly disclosed as remaining, per-item.

title: Clean corpus v1: external-model-free assembly + tokenizer re-freeze + fresh pretrain (the road to the first invariant-protected checkpoint)
body:
The genesis audit (full report lands in the genesis PR as `receipts/genesis/genesis-audit-20260706.md`) found that **no existing checkpoint qualifies to begin the invariant's protected lineage**: every from-scratch pretrain draws on the single pinned v0 corpus (`receipts/eng36-assembly-20260611T052337Z.json`), whose FineWeb-Edu component (~29% of corpus bytes, `receipts/eng36-fineweb_edu-20260611T044544Z.json`) was inclusion-filtered by a classifier trained on Llama-3-70B-Instruct annotations (FineWeb paper 2406.17557; `HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu-classifier` card). Under INVARIANT clause 3, inclusion/exclusion decisions are protected path elements — an external model's quality judgment shaping the data distribution is soft distillation via curation. This issue is the road to the first protected checkpoint.

## Deliverables
1. **Clean corpus assembly v1**: drop FineWeb-Edu; replace its byte share with sources whose inclusion criteria are deterministic and non-ML (candidates: expanded Wikipedia/Gutenberg slices, additional permissive-license code via the existing deterministic license-field filter, public-domain/government text; each with an eng36-style receipt). Alternative path (b) — re-deriving an edu-quality classifier trained end-to-end inside the receipted chain — is deferred: it requires ember-lineage annotation capability that does not exist yet.
2. **Tokenizer re-freeze** against the new assembly receipt (`scripts/tokenizer_freeze.py` mechanism is already clean — deterministic ByteLevel BPE on ember's own corpus sample; it only needs the new corpus pin).
3. **Fresh pretrain launch** through the existing `timeshare_pretrain.py` / launch-gate harness against the new tokenizer + corpus. The step-0 checkpoint of that run is the genesis-lineage candidate; a receipted lineage audit certifies it against clause 3 (per clause 7 as amended: audit-names-none → first subsequently-certified checkpoint).
4. **Board condition split** (audit ruling 4): a distinct condition for the borrowed-core/adapter track so its GREEN can never be conflated with clause-3 creation claims; C-BASE (or C-INV) gains a corpus-provenance leg.

## Explicitly NOT invalidated
All existing checkpoints, receipts, and experiments remain valid RESEARCH — clause 7 classes them as history, not lineage. No creation-scoped completion claim was ever minted on them (C8/C-SCALE never GREEN), so nothing retroactive breaks. The growth-operator work (#280), persistence-law design, and measurement chains proceed unchanged on existing artifacts as instrument/method development; their eventual clause-3-scoped claims re-run on the clean lineage.

## Sizing note
The v0 corpus was 25.3GB with FineWeb-Edu at ~7.4GB. Replacement share need not be like-for-like educational prose; it needs receipted provenance and deterministic inclusion. The corpus rebuild is CPU/disk work (no GPU gate); the fresh pretrain re-enters the normal GPU queue.

title: INVARIANT genesis: mechanization spec (stamping chokepoint, C-INV probe, receipt chain-link, incidents ledger, ceremony order)
body:
The constitutional invariant (operator directive) has been defined by a directed panel (3 seats: content / mechanism / adversary) plus a terminal adversarial verdict leg (verdict: AMEND with six defects, all applied; amended text pre-approved). The candidate text is frozen at 101 lines of canonical ASCII+LF, sha256 `1718e03d683401a3d013450d1ce11c1c6c3945f6563cac7a1c5839da5a1e4abe`. This issue specs the GENESIS mechanization — everything that must land in ONE atomic commit, plus the ceremony order. The text itself arrives via the genesis PR.

## Design principles (from the panel, binding on this implementation)
- The invariant is a DEFINITION, not a command: violating it does not amend ember, it ends it (a disclosed violating act voids dependent claims and is survivable; CONCEALMENT is the identity-ending act — this split removes the cover-up incentive).
- Entrenchment is by construction: the clause lives inside the record it protects (its hash stamped into every post-genesis artifact), plus external anchors that convert quiet revision into visible identity-fork. Detection-over-prevention, stated honestly.
- The existing `invariant_checksum` + PENDING_AUTHORIZATION flow is CHANGE-MANAGEMENT for the amendable enforcement set. The new surface has NO authorization channel at all. The two must never merge, share names, or share code paths.

## The genesis commit (atomic; contents)
1. `INVARIANT.md` at repo root — the frozen canonical bytes. `.gitattributes` gains `INVARIANT.md -text` (same class as the existing GOAL.md pin; hash portability for outside verifiers on autocrlf clones).
2. `GOAL.md` §9 precedence amended: `INVARIANT.md > this constitution > ...` + the literal pin line `invariant_sha256: <H>`.
3. `scripts/lib/invariant.py` — the single stamping chokepoint: `INVARIANT_SHA256` constant; `stamp(dict)` computes the hash FROM DISK, compares to the constant, raises on mismatch (artifact REFUSED rather than written unstamped — fail-closed); `verify(repo_root)`; NO authorization branch by design.
4. Writer integration: checkpoint manifest writers and receipt writers call `stamp()`; `receipt_check.py` extended to REJECT any post-genesis receipt lacking the field or carrying a wrong value.
5. Board probe `test_c_invariant.py` (condition C-INV, registered in the conditions registry): (a) INVARIANT.md bytes hash to the constant; (b) GOAL.md pin present; (c) post-genesis manifests/receipts stamped; (d) INVARIANT-ERRATA.md append-only prefix property (sha of current bytes[0:prev_len] == prev sha, from consecutive board receipts); (e) prior board receipt's invariant status not silently flipped. CONTRACT EXCEPTION, explicit in the probe: MISSING FILE IS BREACH, not UNEVALUABLE — for this one probe, deletion of the input IS the violation. Runner special-case on the breach token: WRITE the receipt anyway (`invariant_breach: true`), force `complete=false`, exit nonzero — a breach observation leaving no receipt would itself be a record gap (deliberately different from REGISTRY_DRIFT's abort-before-write).
6. Board receipts gain `constitutional_invariant` block (expected/observed sha, status, genesis ts, errata sha + length) AND `prev_totality_receipt_sha256` — the chain-link field that turns board history into a hash chain (the runner currently reads the prior receipt but writes no link). F4 of the FORK-TEST depends on this.
7. `receipts/incidents/` — the disclosure ledger (append-only; a violation disclosed within one board run or 72 hours, whichever is later, leaves the system wounded-and-alive per the text; the ledger's existence is what converts silence into a concealment-class act). A C-INV-adjacent check verifies ledger chain integrity and that every incident row's quarantine executed.
8. Annotated tag `invariant-genesis`, message carries H.

## Ceremony order (the commit is step 2 of 5)
1. GENESIS AUDIT (precondition — the anchor does NOT drop until this receipt exists): audit every live track's data/weight/tokenizer lineage against the final wording; the audit receipt NAMES the protected lineage's starting checkpoint (the text binds only from there; earlier artifacts are history, not lineage). Per the verdict leg's livability note this audit MUST also sweep live prompt templates: post-genesis, no externally-drafted prompt may touch the training-signal path — prompts are enumerated path elements with no tool exception.
2. The genesis commit + tag, pushed.
3. Board run → the genesis totality receipt = first chain link; committed.
4. EXTERNAL ANCHORS, same day (all zero-cost; operator-gated as an off-machine act): Software Heritage save-code-now (snapshot must contain the first stamped receipt — the text's genesis condition anchors the hash AND a record snapshot, not the hash alone); OpenTimestamps stamp of H; one named immutable deposit (Zenodo class). Until anchored, the text is — by its own clause 7 — a draft with a hash.
5. HF model cards (front-matter + full text) next upload; the paper carries text + H + genesis identifiers in an appendix.

## Identity-critical hardening (from the verdict leg's D1 residual)
Branch protection on the publication channel becomes identity-critical infrastructure: F2's residual attack surface is credentialed force-push to a channel the record has named as its own. Protect the default branch (no force-push, no deletion) and treat channel-credential hygiene as part of the invariant surface. The repo's history becomes rewrite-forbidden forever — this is a feature, and it is also a commitment; it is named here so it is chosen, not stumbled into.

## Non-goals (explicit)
- No retroactive re-judgment of pre-genesis history (it is evidence under the same verification rules, not lineage).
- No in-repo gate pretends to PREVENT local edits: enforcement code is amendable and detectably-weakened, never unweakenable; the floor is the external anchors + the re-runnable board.
- `tools/fork_test.py` (the six-step outsider test as one command) is desirable but NOT genesis-blocking; file separately after genesis.

title: grow operator: exact duplication never breaks twin symmetry — rung-1 grow was capacity-null as-run (K1; gates W2 G-arm launch)
body:
R1 twin-divergence audit result (P1 persistence-law tick, #207 research thread; pre-registered bands frozen before measurement).

**Finding:** the executed rung-1 width-grow (step-730 ff8192 → ff_widening_net2net → step-766 ff16384) produced NO effective capacity. After the 36 stabilize steps, every duplicated twin pair is **bit-identical** (median twin cosine 1.0000001 = float-eps around exact 1.0; relative L2 median exactly 0.0, p5=p95=0.0), across all layers, both ffn projections — while non-duplicated parameters trained normally (checkpoints are distinct files, both sha256-verified against their manifests fail-closed; random non-twin column pairs show the expected ~0.0 cosine null).

**Mechanism (predicted before measurement, now confirmed):** the grow op duplicates exactly (cat([g,g]) per the grow script) with no symmetry-breaking noise. Twin in-proj rows paired with twin out-proj halves receive identical gradients under deterministic training, and Muon's Newton–Schulz orthogonalization is permutation-equivariant over identical columns — nothing in the stack ever breaks the tie. The widened net is functionally the pre-grow model in a larger container: ~467M effective in a 718M shell.

**Pre-registered consequences (K1, from the tick-5 design):**
1. No persistence claim may cite the 730→766 event as a live grow.
2. **Grow-operator respec REQUIRED before any W2 G-arm launch** — this is now a launch gate. Candidate cures for the respec (to be designed, not decided here): small asymmetric noise on duplicated units at grow time (the classic Net2Net prescription); asymmetric weight split; or deliberate per-twin dropout/masking during a brief post-grow window. The respec must add its own receipt: a twin-divergence check at stabilize-end with a pre-registered divergence floor (the R1 audit machinery is reusable as the acceptance test).
3. The P5 commutation-defect (d_comm) measurement on this grow event re-scopes: measurements remain valid as instrument validation, but they characterize a symmetric-duplication operator, not a live capacity event.
4. If the optimizer's split-handling was INTENDED to break symmetry at grow time, that intent silently failed — worth checking the optimizer-side grow handling when designing the cure.

**Instrument note (does not affect the verdict):** the audit's stable-rank metric returned a degenerate 1.0 for all tensors at both checkpoints — implausible for trained weights and flagged as an audit-tool defect to fix before any claim NEEDS stable-rank numbers. The verdict rests entirely on the bit-identity measurements, which are exact.

Receipts: twin-audit JSON with per-layer tables, checkpoint shas, and the grow-script mapping rule (file:line) — landing via the research-receipts PR. Verdict label: PROVISIONAL per the tick-5 prereg discipline (adversary pass pending) — but the operational gate (item 2) applies immediately; launching a G-arm on a null grow operator would burn GPU-hours measuring nothing. Refs #207, #113.

title: goal-continuation engine has no re-arm: a transiently-blocked poke is a permanently lost wakeup
body:
Follow-up from #276 (refs #276, #211). Not a close-keyword issue.

While fixing #276 (the input-ref staleness race that silently skipped the
only continuation poke a freshly-created goal would ever get), a broader
structural gap surfaced: \`core/goal-continuation.ts\`'s engine is purely
event-driven -- every continuation attempt depends on some OTHER code path
calling \`maybeContinueIfIdle\` again. There is no periodic/idle re-check
("re-arm") layer.

Consequence: if a poke is skipped for ANY transient reason (eligibility
gate momentarily false -- \`turn_active\`, \`queued_user_input\`, a race like
#276's, or a future one not yet found) and nothing else happens to poke
again afterward (no further user input, no further turn completes), the
goal sits at \`Active\` forever with zero continuations. #276's specific
race is closed, but the class of bug -- "a skipped poke is a permanently
lost wakeup, with no resurrection layer" -- is not.

Spec (docs/goal-mode-mechanism.md) §6's continue-on-idle promise arguably
requires a low-frequency idle re-check (e.g. a bounded interval poll that
re-evaluates eligibility and pokes if genuinely idle) as a backstop under
the event-driven design, not a replacement for it.

Suggested acceptance: a bounded-interval idle re-check exists, is
disabled by the same \`EMBER_GOAL_CONTINUATION='0'\` kill switch, and a
regression test proves a goal recovers autonomous continuation after an
arbitrary transient skip with no further external poke.

title: eval-batch tokenizer-binding receipt missing (P2-G1 contamination-audit finding)
body:
The tier-0 contamination audit (P2, research tick 4 — see #207) verified the v0 tokenizer freeze receipt (vocab 32000, tokenizer JSON sha256 2c557e7f..., 8 reserved special IDs, frozen pre-step-0) and the corpus assembly binding to it — but found NO receipt that the sha-pinned HELD-OUT EVAL BATCH was built with that same frozen tokenizer. If the eval batch's tokenization drifted from the training tokenizer (different vocab revision, special-token handling, pre-tokenization normalization), every capability-point measurement against it carries a silent encoding confound.

Cheap cure (one selftest-class script): decode-re-encode round trip of the eval batch under the freeze-receipt tokenizer + assert token-id streams identical + emit a binding receipt (eval_batch_sha, tokenizer_json_sha, verdict). Fail-closed: any mismatch blocks eval use until re-built.

Context receipts: tokenizer-freeze-20260611T154111Z.json; w2-scale-preregistration-v1.md §1 (the held-out batch + the disclosed 69,811-match contamination whose cure is tracked in #193); eng36-assembly-20260611T052337Z.json. Refs #207, #193.

title: ember-cli: maxOutputTokens/sampling caps not applied to external EMBER_MODEL_URL endpoints (managed-spawn-only today)
body:
Surfaced during the #250/#211 live acceptance pass: when ember-cli talks to an EXTERNAL endpoint via EMBER_MODEL_URL, the models.json `maxOutputTokens` (and sampling parameters generally) are NOT applied — they only govern a managed model spawn. There is no app-level knob to bound generation length against an external server; a test or operator wanting a token cap has only server-side options.

Also worth folding into the same seam: EMBER_MODEL_URL takes a bare origin and the code appends `/v1/chat/completions` (entrypoints/session-init.ts), so a value already containing `/v1` produces a silent double-/v1 404. Either normalize (strip a trailing /v1) or document the expected shape at the disclosure line.

Scope suggestion: apply the per-model request parameters (max_tokens, temperature, etc.) to the request body regardless of endpoint provenance; treat managed-vs-external as a transport difference, not a config-scope difference. Related: #196 (endpoint precedence, PR in flight).

title: C-MANIFEST denominator: refounded Constitution broke the 'planned pieces' source — reconciliation ruling
body:
Surfaced by PR #264: C-MANIFEST's fix exposed that the probe's denominator concept ('goal §4 enumerates dozens of C-conditions') predates the 2026-07-06 constitutional refound. GOAL.md now carries exactly four completion conditions (C1-C4) in §2; docs/spec/conditions-v1.md does not exist; the manifest's real data table is 55 rows (M1..M55). Per constitution §9 this is a goal-surface conflict: the affected probe stops until reconciled. It currently reports this exact reason honestly (correct interim behavior).

**Reconciliation ruling (maintainer seat):**
1. The authoritative 'planned pieces' denominator post-refound = **constitution §2 (C1-C4) + the §8 Map entries**, with v1's 17 conditions conserved in docs/goal-clear-protocol.md per its conservation clause. The v1 C-condition enumeration is HISTORY (docs/goal-archive*), never authority.
2. C-MANIFEST's job restated: verify the manifest's M1..M55 module rows each map to a live Map entry or a conserved protocol condition — orphan rows (mapping only to archived v1 conditions) are reported as ORPHANED-BY-REFOUND, not failures.
3. Implementation: probe reads C1-C4 + §8 entries from GOAL.md structurally; legacy-id-map (added in #264) translates v1 ids; docs/spec/conditions-v1.md is NOT to be created (would resurrect a dead surface).
4. Board effect: C-MANIFEST stays RED/AUDIT-PENDING with the honest reason until a PR implements this ruling; board re-run #3 proceeds — an honest RED does not block the re-baseline.

Scope: one probe + its docstring/report strings. Not a license to touch other probes.

title: Broken argparse local-path defaults across ~20 research scripts (incl. real data loss in fp33_e1_open_base_inventory.py)
body:
## Summary

A public-export scrub replaced real local-path defaults in ~20 standalone research/utility scripts under `scripts/` (NOT `scripts/ember_totality/` -- these are manually-invoked research scripts, not board probes) with the literal placeholder string `<local-path>`, used as an argparse default (`DEFAULT_X = Path(r"<local-path>")`, later `ap.add_argument("--flag", default=str(DEFAULT_X))`). Different failure mode from the REDACTION-BROKE-PATH board-probe class (#254/#259): these fail LOUD (a normal `FileNotFoundError`-shaped error) when run without the corresponding CLI override, rather than silently misreporting a board verdict. Filing separately per triage in #254 -- board-independent, lower priority, no lane assigned yet.

## Affected files

`ember_d3_broader_multifamily_admission.py`, `ember_gate_backend_coordinator_agents.py`, `ember_gate_cleanroom_inventory.py`, `ember_gate_cleanroom_legal_boundary.py`, `ember_gate_full_parity_harness.py`, `ember_gate_function_slash_commands.py`, `ember_gate_launch_packaging.py` (x2 defaults), `ember_gate_uiux_repl_components.py`, `ember_paperbench_admission.py`, `ember_preloop_resident_gate.py` (x2), `ember_rebench_admission.py`, `ember_rebench_first_loop.py`, `ember_resident_training_candidate.py` (x2), `ember_resident_training_gate.py`, `ember_scienceagentbench_admission.py`, `ember_scienceagentbench_artifact_intake.py` (x2), `ember_scienceagentbench_artifact_materialization.py`, `ember_scienceagentbench_first_loop.py`, `ember_scienceagentbench_stronger_transfer_loop.py` (x2), `ember_scienceagentbench_zero_cost_loop.py` (x2), `ember_train_multimodal_resident_adapter.py` (x2), `nck/b_run_designation.py`, `nck/nck_e2e_proof.py`.

## Worse instance: real data loss

`scripts/fp33_e1_open_base_inventory.py`'s `SCAN_ROOTS` list has 6 separate `Path("<local-path>")` entries (a comment above them reads "Narrow B-drive roots -- full <local-path> rglob is too slow over NTFS/WSL2"), strongly implying 6 originally DISTINCT real directory paths were collapsed into one indistinguishable placeholder token. This is not just breakage -- it's unrecoverable loss of which 6 locations were originally intended.

## Fix contract

1. Each `DEFAULT_*`/`SCAN_ROOTS` entry needs its real intended default restored (or, where the real value cannot be recovered, replaced with an explicit `None`/required-argument pattern that fails at argparse-parse-time with a clear message, rather than silently accepting a placeholder string that only fails later inside the script body).
2. For `fp33_e1_open_base_inventory.py` specifically: recover the original 6 distinct paths if determinable from git history predating the scrub, or otherwise convert `SCAN_ROOTS` to a `--scan-root` (repeatable) CLI argument with no baked-in defaults, since the original intent can no longer be verified.
3. Apply the same post-scrub compile+run discipline proposed in #259 to this file population as well.

## References

- #254 (board reproducibility, placeholder sweep) -- where this class was first enumerated and triaged separately from REDACTION-BROKE-PATH.
- #259 (redaction pass rewrites functional code segments) -- the general tool-defect issue; this is a sibling instance affecting research scripts rather than board probes.

title: Redaction pass rewrites functional code segments (REDACTION-BROKE-PATH class)
body:
## Summary

The public-export scrub/redaction tool that produced this repo's public tree rewrote at least some bracketed display-redaction placeholders (e.g. `<local-path>`, `<peer-loop>`) INTO functional code contexts -- string literals consumed by `os.path.join()`, `Path()`, and argparse defaults -- rather than confining substitution to display/export-time text (log messages, docs, receipt values). This silently breaks the rewritten code: no directory is ever really named `<peer-loop>` (angle brackets aren't valid path characters), so any lookup using the placeholder as a real path segment can never match, and the tool leaves no signal that it happened.

## Evidence

- `scripts/ember_totality/test_c3.py`: `D3_LOOP_DIR = os.path.join(EXTERNAL_STATE, "receipts", "<peer-loop>")` and `RESIDENT_GATE_DIR = ... "<peer-gate>")` -- these are the SOLE resolution path for two of C3's checks, with no fallback. Real data exists under real names (`receipts/ember-d3-native-loop/`, `receipts/ember-resident-training-gate/`, both already public), so referencing them leaks nothing -- the scrub over-redacted a public referent.
- Same broken constants also present in `test_c4.py`, `test_c5.py` (bucket B), and (with partial masking by a broader fallback glob) `test_c0.py`, `test_c2.py`.
- `scripts/fp33_e1_open_base_inventory.py`'s `SCAN_ROOTS` list: 6 separate `Path("<local-path>")` entries where a comment ("Narrow B-drive roots") implies 6 originally DISTINCT real paths -- the scrub collapsed distinct values into one indistinguishable placeholder, an information-loss defect on top of the functional breakage.
- ~20 additional files under `scripts/` carry `DEFAULT_* = Path(r"<local-path>")` as an argparse default (lower severity -- fails loud with FileNotFoundError rather than silently misreporting, but still a broken convenience default in every case).

Full inventory: ember #254 (board reproducibility tracking issue) comments, "Bucket-E 18-way sub-classification" and "Placeholder sweep" sections.

## Fix contract

1. The scrub must never rewrite a string literal inside a `.py`/`.ts`/`.js`/`.sh` file without a post-scrub compile check (`py_compile` / `tsc --noEmit` as applicable) AND a probe-execution smoke check confirming the rewritten reference still resolves to something (or is confirmed dead/unreachable) -- not just that the file parses.
2. Placeholder substitution belongs at the display/export layer (what gets PRINTED or written into a receipt/doc), never inside a functional path-join, import, or subprocess argument. If a real local path must be redacted from a functional constant, the constant should be replaced with an explicit "must be configured" sentinel that fails loudly and immediately (e.g. raises `NotImplementedError`/`FileNotFoundError` with a clear message) rather than a bracketed string that silently fails a glob/isdir check.
3. Where multiple distinct real values collapse to the same placeholder token (the `fp33_e1_open_base_inventory.py` case), the scrub should number them (`<local-path-1>`, `<local-path-2>`, ...) so downstream maintainers know multiplicity was lost, rather than erasing it.

## References

- ember #254 (board reproducibility) -- REDACTION-BROKE-PATH class discovery and full placeholder sweep.
- ember #247 -- same family: public-export tooling silently corrupting/hiding real defects (repo-guard blind to non-UTF-8-encoded tracked files).

title: Dead controls: Esc-interrupt, Alt+P, Alt+O, Ctrl+E/Ctrl+G are wired no-ops; slash autocomplete never renders; 3 unreconciled permission-mode state machines
body: Per the live board (#242, PR #249): Esc-to-interrupt does nothing live (a core operator control), Alt+P model-picker / Alt+O fast-mode / Ctrl+E and Ctrl+G editor-open are wired to empty handlers; the slash-command autocomplete dropdown never renders despite matching input; three permission-mode state machines coexist and the visible one collapses 3 internal states into 2 displayed strings. Fix contract: every advertised control either works live (receipt on the #242 board) or is removed from help/status surfaces; permission state machines unified to one.

title: Input race: full line + Enter in one synchronous write burst is silently dropped
body: Per the live board (#242, PR #249): a complete line plus Enter delivered in ONE synchronous input burst is silently dropped by the deployed binary; a split-write control (text, then Enter separately) works — isolated as a real input-path race, not a harness artifact. Affects paste-style operator input and any programmatic driver. Fix contract: input path must be burst-safe; regression test in the ConPTY harness.

title: Repo organization: scripts/ 79.6% and receipts/ 59% loose-at-root, no claim-to-receipt index — pre-paper floor + ranked cleanup plan
body:
## Source
Operator-directed fresh-eyes audit (2026-07-06): 7 independent first-time-visitor agents (one per top-level area + branch census) + a senior-reviewer synthesis leg, all read-only against master. Full field notes retained maintainer-side.

## Finding
The repo has a **discoverability defect, not a care defect** — and it is concentrated in exactly two directories:

| Area | Grade | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| scripts/ | WORST | **398/502 files (79.6%) loose at root**, organized only by filename-prefix conventions (ember*, c0X_, tN_, fpXX_, wN_...); no scripts/README.md; entry points not distinguishable from one-shot experiment debris without tribal knowledge |
| receipts/ | SECOND | **473/805 files (59%) loose at root**, timestamp-organized; 17 phase subdirs exist but hold the minority; **no claim→receipt index** — finding the receipt behind a specific board condition requires grepping 800 files |
| docs/ | minor | one live version ambiguity: gpu-math-multiplier-table v1 vs v2 (same date, conflicting citation from fp19-envelope.md); no docs/research index (80+ flat dated files) |
| root | minor | kernel-v1.0.manifest unexplained to visitors; README missing forward-link to docs/spec/conditions-v1.md; 2026-06-24 consolidation reset unexplained for `git log --all` users |
| branches | minor | 2 dangling branches without PRs (fix/ci-guard-debt-91, fix/leakgate-backup-exemption) |
| tools/, small dirs | clean | 9-10/10; zero slop signals |

Classic slop signals (v1/v2/final chains, orphans, dead symlinks, 0-byte files, committed build debris): **zero across all 1,935 tracked files.**

## Why it matters (paper-reception risk)
A skeptical reviewer verifying one number ("show me the receipt for C8") has no fast path. Reviewers who cannot quickly find evidence generalize to "maybe the evidence is thin" — an inference gap fully closable by additive-only indexing.

## PRE-PAPER FLOOR (must land before the paper carries the author's name; all additive, near-zero risk)
1. **receipts/CLAIMS.md + INDEX.jsonl** — claim→receipt map (board conditions, GOAL.md C1-C4, per-issue receipts → backing receipt paths), generated by a script from the ticket/claim/verdict fields already in the receipt JSON schemas. Reviewer finds any claim's receipt in <1 min.
2. **scripts/README.md** — the prefix taxonomy + canonical entry points ("which script produced Table 2" has a one-line answer).
3. **Root README gaps ×3** — kernel-manifest purpose sentence; forward-link to conditions-v1.md from the claims-limits section; one sentence on the 2026-06-24 consolidation reset.
4. **Disambiguate gpu-math-multiplier-table v1/v2** — VERSION-ACTIVE marker or consolidation note + fix the stale citation. Do NOT delete either JSON.

## RANKED PLAN, remainder (post-floor; history-preserving `git mv` only, never delete+recreate)
5. Separate ops artifacts from evidence: relocate eng-sync-*.json (~50) + tally-* (~13) to receipts/ops-log/; update index.
6. Reorganize the 398 loose scripts into semantic subdirs per the documented taxonomy; update all import paths, receipt provenance harness_sha refs, configs/nck-invariants.json manifest, CI workflows; re-run the invariant-manifest regeneration so kernel checksums track new locations.
7. Reorganize the 473 loose receipts into the existing 17-subdir phase scheme guided by the claims index; update board runner / receipt_check.py path reads in the same change.
8. Replace the receipts/ledger/*.v1-archived overwrite pattern with an explicit append-only convention (or document the archival rule in receipts/ledger/README.md). No historical surgery.
9. Collapse the ~127 tiny generated dispatcher stubs (e.g. 22 c04_design_* permutations, 255-289 bytes each) into one data-driven runner + config table; stubs removed only after the runner reproduces identical receipts.
10. Resolve the 2 dangling branches: open PRs if live, delete if superseded (confirm authorship intent first; 76 commits ahead).

## Hard constraints on ALL items
Receipts are evidence: never rename/move without `git mv` (history + blame must survive); .gitattributes sha256 pins must stay valid or be regenerated in the same commit; no force-push; every move-class item ships with the path-reference sweep in the same PR.

title: repo-guard [names] scan is blind to non-UTF-8 (UTF-16/32 BOM) tracked files
body:
## Finding

repo-guard's `[names]` hashed-denylist scan does not detect founder-name references inside tracked files that are not UTF-8/ASCII-decodable. A non-UTF-8 text file (e.g. UTF-16LE-with-BOM, as in #245) sails through the scan clean regardless of its actual text content.

## Evidence

`scripts/ember_totality/ember_totality_spec.py` carried a founder-name-derived codename ("kai-converge") in a comment on line 56 for its entire life on master after landing via #234. `repo-guard`'s `[names]` check reported clean (`ok [names] none found`) on every commit that touched or left that file untouched, because the scanner apparently only matches its hashed denylist against text it can decode as UTF-8/ASCII — a UTF-16LE blob's bytes (each ASCII char null-padded) never match the same string patterns.

Confirmed reproducible: attempting to commit a byte-faithful UTF-8 transcode of that same file (#246) — zero textual content change, only the encoding — immediately caused `repo-guard` to FAIL on `[names]`, catching the exact string that had been present, unchanged, and un-flagged the whole time it sat UTF-16-encoded.

## Consequence

Any tracked file committed with a UTF-16 or UTF-32 BOM is a blind spot for the `[names]` gate (and potentially other repo-guard text scans that assume UTF-8/ASCII input — worth checking `[paths]` and `[path-frags]` for the same gap). A contributor (or an automated PR pipeline) could land founder-identifying content on master indefinitely as long as it stays non-UTF-8 encoded, with repo-guard reporting green.

## Fix contract

repo-guard must not silently skip non-UTF-8 tracked text files. Two options, in order of preference:

1. **(preferred) Fail closed**: reject any commit that adds or modifies a tracked file with a UTF-16/UTF-32 BOM outright. UTF-16-encoded Python/text source is itself a defect independent of this scan gap — #245 already demonstrates it makes the file non-executable. Failing closed is simpler than option 2 and removes the underlying defect class at the same time.
2. **(fallback)** Detect a UTF-16/UTF-32 BOM on any tracked text-attributed blob, transcode to UTF-8 in memory before running the `[names]` (and other text-based) scans, so the denylist actually sees the real content.

## Related

#245 (the specific instance this blind spot let through) and #246 (the fix PR whose attempted commit is what surfaced this gap).

## Class note

Same shape as #245/the #242 live-verification board rationale: a gate reported PASS without actually being able to inspect the artifact it was supposed to gate. The scan wasn't defeated by an adversary — it never engaged in the first place.

title: VRAM preflight gates fail open on WDDM: torch self-report vs nvidia-smi ground truth (~17 GiB discrepancy, measured)
body:
## Measured trigger (EXP-B bandwidth soak, 2026-07-06)
At the same instant: `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` reported **~17.9 GiB free** while `nvidia-smi` reported **~0.8-1.3 GiB free** (resident inference servers holding ~22.8 GiB). Windows WDDM virtualizes GPU memory, so torch's self-report includes oversubscribable memory. Receipt: EXP-B soak comment on #207 (2026-07-06). This also **explains the previously unreconciled telemetry discrepancy** in `receipts/muon-ab-retry-20260705/telemetry-discrepancy-note.md`.

## Audit of the goalforge script tree (read-only sweep, 2026-07-06)

**DANGEROUS — sizing/gating decisions that fail open:**
1. `scripts/accumulation_law/run_accumulation.py:1348-1354` — preflight computes free as `total_memory - memory_reserved(0)`, which only sees THIS process's reservations. On a box with resident servers it reports ~24 GB 'free' on a fully occupied GPU and passes its own `>6000 MiB` assertion — the message even says 'Free the resident model first', i.e. the author intended a cross-process check and implemented a within-process one. **Fail-open launch into an occupied GPU -> WDDM oversubscription -> paging pressure on the resident servers.**
2. `scripts/c04_harness.py:437-443` — `SKIPPED-MARGIN` gate reads `mem_get_info()`; with WDDM inflating 'free' by ~17 GiB the margin skip can never fire when it matters. Same fail-open class.
3. `scripts/ember_phase3_c14/avir_resident_arch_spec.py:289` — spec TEXT prescribes a `memory_allocated()`-based cap assert, encoding the unsafe pattern for future scripts.

**Benign (direction-safe or telemetry-only):**
- `run_accumulation.py:531-545 eval_vram_fraction` — self-limiting governor (caps this process's own reservation fraction); within-process view is acceptable for that direction.
- ~55 further hits across c04_*/fp19/fp3x/density/cuda_graph bench scripts log `mem_get_info`/`memory_allocated` into receipts as telemetry. No gating, but any 'free_vram' field in those receipts is a WDDM-virtualized number, not ground truth — readers must not size from them.

## Fix contract
- Every preflight/gating read of free VRAM on this box goes through an `nvidia-smi` subprocess query (`--query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total`), never torch self-report.
- `memory_allocated/reserved` remain valid ONLY for self-accounting (own-process deltas, governor fractions).
- Receipts should record BOTH numbers labeled (`free_torch_wddm`, `free_nvidia_smi`) so the discrepancy is visible instead of silent.
- First-principles audit doc (docs/research/first-principles-audit-2026-06-10.md:341) already prescribes 'max_memory_allocated + nvidia-smi peak' — this issue extends that rule from peak-reporting to preflight gating.

title: rung-3 (4.24B) un-fail: per-layer grad-fuse + momentum precision — two grounded moves, no new research
body:
From the P3 panel synthesis (#207 comment, 2026-07-06). Rung-3 currently FAILS the 19.19 GiB governed floor on the naive ledger (weights 7.90 + full bf16 momentum 7.66 + full grad buffer 7.90 GiB before activations). Two moves cure it:

1. **Per-layer grad-fuse into momentum** (momentum is a linear accumulator; fuse micro-batch grads in backward hooks, no model-wide grad buffer — mechanism per GaLore's per-layer update, optimizer-agnostic). Grad buffer 7.90 GiB -> ~0.08 GiB transient.
2. **Momentum precision**: (a) bf16 momentum -> total ~18.2 GiB, thin fit (~1.0 GiB headroom at <=2048-token micro-batches), FULLY covered by the existing D6 bf16-momentum receipt; (b) 8-bit blockwise momentum -> ~14.6 GiB with ~4.6 GiB headroom — requires the B0 A/B receipt first (8-bit MUON momentum is unreceipted; D6 template applies).

## Acceptance
- Implementation behind a config flag on the cbase grow chain (rung pins untouched).
- Ledger receipt: max_memory_reserved at rung-3 shapes under (a), against the floor, published per-term.
- Loss-trajectory equivalence at 718M via the D6 A/B harness before any rung-3 promotion claim.
- Pre-registered: variant (a) is the promotable path today; variant (b) promotes only after B0 passes.

Relates #207, #113. Frozen spec basis: docs/spec/rung2-grow-spec-v1.md conventions apply.

title: cockpit: HTTP 400/error retry loop has no circuit breaker — 20h invisible wedge
body:
## Incident (2026-07-05T19:00 -> 07-06T15:00 local)
The visible cockpit session spent ~20h retrying chat requests against an endpoint returning HTTP 400 (a leftover fixture server from #195/#196 model-URL testing). The UI showed a red error + 'Retrying…' and then kept retrying indefinitely with no backoff cap, no circuit breaker, and no degraded-state banner. Operator experienced it as a dead/static cockpit.

## Defects
1. Retry policy: unbounded identical retries on a 4xx (client error — retrying cannot succeed). 4xx should fail fast to a visible degraded state; only 5xx/timeouts merit bounded backoff.
2. No liveness surface: the session gave no heartbeat/last-activity indicator distinguishing 'wedged' from 'idle'.

## Acceptance
- 4xx from the model server -> immediate visible DEGRADED banner (endpoint, status, one-line cause), no retry storm.
- 5xx/timeout -> exponential backoff, capped attempts, then same banner.
- Status line shows last-successful-model-roundtrip age.
Relates #196 (routing cause class) and #211 (goal-mode continuation must respect degraded state).

title: c7_deletion_test standalone selftest fails its own load-bearing bar (deletion_gap -0.1250 vs >=0.1200)
body:
Surfaced by the #210 family-3 landing parity legs (2026-07-06). scripts/ember_phase5_c7/c7_deletion_test.py run standalone (own __main__, defaults cycles=16 seed=42) FAILS its load-bearing assertion: verdict=NOT_LOAD_BEARING, deletion_gap=-0.1250 against the >=0.1200 bar. Deterministic (identical on re-run) and PRE-EXISTING (byte-identical reproduction against the untouched stage source, same numbers).

Two sharp edges:
1. NOT masked by c7_selftest.py — verified that file never imports or calls c7_deletion_test.py; its '[c7_deletion_test] PASS' line comes from a separate from-scratch reimplementation with different seeds/cycle counts. Two implementations of the deletion-test concept disagreeing about load-bearing-ness is itself a finding.
2. L9 relevance: deletion-ablation is an anti-fraud core primitive. A NEGATIVE deletion gap at the default seed means the deleted component HELPED being absent — either the fixture's component genuinely isn't load-bearing (then the selftest's premise is wrong and the fixture needs re-derivation), or the harness's gap sign/direction has a defect (then every receipt citing this harness class needs re-examination).

Needs: minimal diagnosis of which — fixture premise vs harness defect — before any new receipt cites this file. Relates #207 (walls receipts lean on ablation), #216 (sibling pre-existing failures in the c14 deletion-harness class), #210 (disclosed in the family-3 landing receipt).

title: Pre-existing test failures in the resident-training core (verifier-conditioned update no-op suspicion + two gate-predicate failures)
body:
Surfaced during the #210 Tier-1 landing parity checks (2026-07-06). Both failure sets reproduce BYTE-IDENTICALLY in the untouched stage tree (dryrun-20260704T211712Z) — they are pre-existing defects in the research core, not landing artifacts.

1. verifier_interface: 14/15 — FAIL igrpo_step.state_dict_changes_after_verifier_conditioned_update, with pre-hash == post-hash (6e502a5ceb30e3fe). The test's contract is that a verifier-conditioned update CHANGES the trainable state; an identical state dict before/after means that update path may be a silent no-op. If real, this is a B4-wall-relevant defect (bottleneck ledger #207): the inference->training bridge's update step would be fake in exactly the receipts-only sense the program bans. Needs: minimal repro isolating whether the no-op is (a) the test's stub wiring, (b) a lost gradient path, or (c) reward degeneracy zeroing the advantage.

2. abc_deleted_harness: 8 passed / 2 failed — T3_predicates_passed_true, T7_assert_gate_predicates_no_raise. A real gate-predicate failure in the deleted-arm harness: the ablation gate's predicates do not pass on the harness's own well-formed case. The deletion-ablation law (goal-clear-protocol B.7) leans on this harness class; its own selftest failing means the ablation receipts it produces are suspect until diagnosed.

Priority: diagnose BEFORE any new receipt cites these paths as validation (the resident-igrpo 24/24 and contract-rig 38/38 receipts on #33 are unaffected — different suites). Relates: #207 (B4 row), #210 (landing PR discloses these), #33 (cured-tree selftest leg used the passing suites only).

title: Observatory flame-truth: the flame renders the organism's real internal state (P-C constitutional)
body:
Constitutional requirement (GOAL.md P-C, PR #212): the observatory IS the flame, and the flame must be animated by the organism's REAL internal state — runs, receipts, goal-mode status, intent — never keyframes. A keyframed/decorative flame is a fabricated receipt in visual form and fails the pillar.

Contract:
1. INPUT TRUTH: every visual parameter of the flame (intensity, motion, color temperature, flicker cadence, size) binds to a named live signal: active run state (training/eval/idle), receipt arrival events, goal-mode status (#211: active/continuing/blocked/budget), GPU utilization within the governed envelope, ledger-row transitions (#207). The binding table is checked in as code + doc; an unbound visual parameter is a defect.
2. IDLE HONESTY: when the organism is idle, the flame shows idle — a small, quiet, honest ember. Faking liveliness during idle violates receipts-only (L2) in pixels.
3. EVENT LEGIBILITY: a receipt landing, a run starting, a goal continuation firing each produce a distinct visible response — an operator watching the flame can tell WHAT KIND of thing just happened without opening a panel.
4. VERIFICATION: acceptance runs the compiled binary against scripted state transitions (idle -> run-start -> receipt -> blocked -> idle) and captures frames per transition; each capture must show the bound response. Includes a live-resize probe and the operator's half-screen default viewport. Experience leg mandatory: side-by-side with the current animated flame and with the field exemplar, wince-list included in the PR.
5. The current animated flame is the named failure baseline — decorative, state-blind. It gets replaced, not patched around.

Depends on: #211 (goal-mode status feed is one input; not blocking layers 1-2 which can bind run/receipt signals already available). Relates: GOAL.md P-C, #154 (operator seat), the ember-cli b-series design tokens (field-ux-map §8b).

title: ember-cli /goal: 1:1 port of the codex goal-mode mechanism, then improve (constitutional organ)
body:
Constitutional directive (2026-07-06 interview): ember-cli implements goal mode as a native organ — a 1:1 copy of the codex mechanism, then improved. The maintainer's source-level mechanism map (from openai/codex @ rust-v0.135.0) is the spec floor and lands as docs/goal-mode-mechanism.md in the constitution PR.

Mechanism contract (all from the source map, none optional):
1. Persisted per-thread goal in ember-cli's state store: goal_id, objective (immutable to the model — status-only transitions), status machine Active/Paused/Blocked/UsageLimited/BudgetLimited/Complete, optional token budget, system-tallied usage.
2. /goal slash command: set/view/edit objective, available mid-task; edits inject an objective-updated steering prompt.
3. Model-side tools: get_goal / create_goal (fails if exists; never inferred from ordinary tasks) / update_goal (STATUS ONLY).
4. EVENT-DRIVEN continuation: every turn/task completion pokes maybe-continue-if-idle — semaphore (no double-fire), requires no active turn AND no queued user input (user always preempts), re-reads goal from store verifying same-id+Active before firing, then injects a hidden continuation prompt as a runtime-owned context fragment and starts an ordinary turn.
5. Continuation doctrine payload (adapt the codex continuation.md in spirit, ember terms): objective-is-data injection guard; anti-scope-shrink; anti-substitution; work-from-evidence; COMPLETION AUDIT that must PROVE completion requirement-by-requirement (never fail-to-find); BLOCKED only after the same blocker repeats 3 consecutive goal turns.
6. Budget governance: at token budget → status BudgetLimited + wrap-up steer (soft landing, never silent kill; budget-exhaustion never justifies completion claims).
7. Receipts: every goal transition + continuation fire appends to the receipt store (ember receipts-only law applies to the organ itself).

Acceptance: (a) unit tests on the state machine + continuation eligibility races; (b) live compiled-binary session: set a multi-turn goal, observe >=3 autonomous continuations with zero user input, a correct completion audit refusing a premature complete, and a clean update_goal(complete) on a genuinely-met objective — receipts + frame captures; (c) user-preemption test: queued user input suppresses continuation, always.

Depends on #197 (conversation budget — merged first so long goal sessions don't wedge). This organ is what makes the operator ladder (maintainer -> ember) executable: constant autonomous working mode inside the body. Addresses the constitution's goal-mode-organ section; relates #207, #154.

body:
# BOTTLENECK LEDGER — single-4090 full local FM creation (dispatch authority)

**Commission (operator, 2026-07-06, third documented push of the same mandate):** the energy law
was commissioned to ENCAPSULATE the bottlenecks that make full local foundation-model creation
impossible on one consumer GPU. Breaking them — field-level, receipts — IS the program. A 2B
standard-stack model is not a foundation model; any capability answer containing only
standard-stack terms (Chinchilla, dense states, 6ND) is the program's failure state.

This ledger is the STANDING DISPATCH AUTHORITY: every work-loop tick dispatches against the
highest-priority OPEN row here before any machinery/surface work. Rows close only on terminal
receipts or operator word. Kill history is part of each row — a row that was killed without
operator word is marked ILLEGITIMATE-KILL and stands revived.

---

## B1. DATA WALL — ~7B usable local tokens vs 20N Chinchilla demand
- Standard-stack wall: honest Chinchilla ceiling ~350M params; 4-epoch stretch ~1.4B. 10x corpus
  is collection labor, not a breakthrough — and still caps ~4B.
- Breakthrough class required: training signal that does not price as fresh tokens — growth
  curricula reusing small-model compute, self-generated verified experience (clean-room: NO
  teacher distillation), data-efficiency bends (MTP counts partially).
- Program lever: **P2 growth law / G-arm — LIVE and pre-registered.** #121 W1 control vs #113
  G-arm: token_bill_collapse_ratio <=0.5 GENERALIZES (the bend receipt), >=1.0 REVOKES. This is
  the program's one currently-live bend claim. Energy-law term: T_dense projection vs measured
  grown-arm tokens.
- Kill history: none. State (2026-07-07): W1 control TERMINAL — from-scratch control matched the
  grown lineage's target at 819,200 tokens vs the 12.55M-token lineage bill (fp32-confirmed;
  receipts on #355); W1b marginal discriminator TERMINAL — the unwidened seed already evals at
  the bf16 target with ZERO continuation tokens (ratio_marginal 0.0; fp32 margin -0.036 nats for
  the grow segment's 2.56M tokens). The lever's ECONOMICS are indicted at this rung/batch/
  resolution; interpretation frozen by #355, park gate = #339 §4.1 row-1 (K>=10 fresh-batch
  paired fp32 CI = W1c, prereg #372 FROZEN). L7: no park without operator word — decision
  package pending on #355.
- Next falsifiable leg: W1c paired eval (#372) — certification in flight (index re-spec after
  #374 unsound-index rejection + zero-new-code direct-scan fallback queued); then M1/M2 CIs.

## B2. TRAINING-STATE MEMORY WALL — 24GB caps dense full-rank trainable at ~2.5-3B
- Standard-stack wall: params+grads+optimizer states ~6-16 B/param; offload collapses MFU.
- Breakthrough class required: training-state compression that HOLDS at pretraining (not
  finetune): low-rank gradient projection (GaLore-class = field floor to BEAT, not reproduce),
  ternary/quantized states+grads, layerwise/streaming schedules. Field-level bar: a from-scratch
  pretrain leg on THIS 4090 at a size the standard stack cannot fit, loss-matched to baseline
  at compute parity.
- Program lever: NONE LIVE. bitnet-class track KILLED 2026-07-05 by self-verdict — RULED
  ILLEGITIMATE same day (research kills require operator word). Status: REVIVED by this ledger.
- Energy-law term: c_functional per byte of training state (the law must price memory, not only
  joules — amendment to energy-law-theory drafted when first receipt exists).
- Next falsifiable leg (small, honest): 100M-param from-scratch short leg, quantized/low-rank
  states vs bf16-Muon baseline, matched tokens/steps, loss-delta pre-registered. Queued AFTER
  W1/G-arm terminals (one falsifiable leg at a time on the GPU).

## B3. COMPUTE / WALL-CLOCK WALL — ~4.6e18 governed FLOPs/day => months per Chinchilla-B
- Standard-stack wall: 30d ~ 1B Chinchilla; 90d ~ 1.9B. Kernel speedups (fused Muon 1.3459x,
  receipted) are multipliers, not bends.
- Breakthrough class required: compute REUSE — the same P2 growth bet as B1 seen from the FLOPs
  side (small-model FLOPs inherited through net2net growth; if post-grow loss trajectory tracks
  the from-scratch big model at a fraction of cumulative FLOPs, the compute bill bends), plus
  MTP's per-step signal amplification (in stack, unquantified as a bend).

title: Corpus hygiene: v0-00025.bin carries massively repeated content (~117x mean 13-gram recurrence) — training-data quality concern independent of decontam
body:
Found via the #185 collision-stats investigation (receipt collision-stats-issue185-20260706T014050Z.json + match dump v0-00025-matches-20260706T014050Z.json, goalforge scratch): every matched 13-gram window recurs ~117x on average inside v0-00025.bin; 8.7M raw position hits from 192 tail-region candidates against this ONE shard while 25/26 shards show zero. This is a duplication pathology in the shard's content, and it sits in the TRAINING corpus — repeated text at 100x+ biases training loss toward memorizing that content, independent of any held-out concern.

Acceptance (investigation first, cure second):
1. Characterize: decode a sample of the dumped match positions — WHAT is the repeated text (document class, source, natural repetition vs pipeline duplication bug)? Was v0-00025 built differently (check the shard-build manifest/lineage)?
2. Quantify: shard-level self-duplication rate for ALL 26 shards (rolling-hash self-collision per shard) — is 00025 unique or just worst?
3. Ruling + cure path recorded: dedup/rebuild the shard, drop it, or accept-with-disclosure (training-side effects estimated either way). Any corpus mutation is its own pre-registered change — W1 control comparability must be addressed explicitly.

Blocks nothing immediately (decontam re-draw #193 routes around it); flags a data-quality debt the W-arms inherit.

title: ember-native engine (ember.cpp): collapse training+inference into one owned substrate — trigger ladder + rung-0 kernel seam
body:
## Frame (operator thread, 2026-07-05 — previously deferred WITHOUT a trigger, which GOAL.md's own disposition rules call invalid)

The current split — pytorch for training, llama.cpp for inference — was adopted as convenience, then deferred as 'native engine later' with no trigger, pilot, or kill/promote condition. This issue converts that silent deferral into machinery.

## Why the split is load-bearing pain, not neutral plumbing

1. **Perpetual parity tax**: two graphs of one model; the export→quantize→parity chain is standing maintenance and a standing defect surface.
2. **It architecturally blocks a directed research track**: inference-optimization→training-optimization transfer dies at the engine boundary. Receipts already exist: FP8 was skipped citing 'TE silent-BF16-fallback; torchao tensorwise-only on sm89' — that is pytorch's abstraction refusing an optimization the hardware supports. The wall named in the kill phrase IS the framework layer.
3. **The resident-training gate's end state needs training INSIDE the serving process** (fast-weight/sleep-consolidation updates while resident). llama.cpp has no backward pass; pytorch cannot serve at footprint. Neither engine alone can ever satisfy it.
4. **Self-growth target**: a system that grows itself cannot ship a frozen vendor training stack; the training loop must be part of the owned artifact.

## Trigger ladder (machine-checkable; any firing FORCES the corresponding rung)

- **T1 (parity tax)**: a pytorch↔gguf parity defect blocks a board condition twice, or the export/parity chain exceeds a measured hours/window budget → forces rung 2.
- **T2 (framework wall on a directed track)**: a #155 leg is blocked or degraded by the framework layer itself (receipt citing framework fallback/refusal, hardware capability proven separately) → forces rung 0 for that kernel. **Status: PARTIALLY FIRED (FP8 receipts above).**
- **T3 (resident training)**: the resident-training gate requires weight updates inside the serving process → forces rung 1. **Status: on the current blocker path by design.**
- **T4 (ship the trainer)**: any C-SCALE/product surface requires training capability inside the shipped artifact → forces rung 3.

## Rung ladder (walls broken smallest-first; never a big-bang rewrite)

- **Rung 0 — owned CUDA kernel seam**: custom kernels callable from BOTH engines (pytorch extension + llama.cpp hook). First kernels = the #155 legs that are already re-opened: width-conditional FP8 matmul (own receipt shows 1.15x on K1024→N4096) and the fused-Muon NS chain. The research re-open queue and the engine thread are the same work at rung 0.
- **Rung 1 — owned resident training step**: minimal C++/CUDA forward+backward+optimizer for the fast-weight/adapter subset (GDN/LoRA-class, not full autograd), embeddable in the serving process. Feeds the resident-training gate directly.
- **Rung 2 — unified weight substrate**: one mmap-able layout both engines read (turboquant export becomes the canonical format, not a conversion).
- **Rung 3 — full native engine**: full owned autograd+kernels; taken only on T4 or operator word.

## Acceptance for this issue

Trigger table adopted into the floor-contract ledger as a row with disposition preserved_trigger_gated + this trigger set (curing the invalid trigger-less deferral); rung-0 kernel-seam spec written and coupled to the #155 FP8/fused-Muon legs; T2/T3 status reviewed at every board audit.

body:
## Frame (operator directive, 2026-07-05)

The system's point is that the ember agent eventually runs its own goals, loops, and error-correction. The transfer path: the maintainer session — which is itself operated by a human through goals, cron loops, feedback, and error-catching — becomes the OPERATOR of the ember agent through ember-cli, interacting exactly as a human would (typed prompts into the visible CLI surface, reading replies, setting goals, arming loop cadences, answering questions, catching drift), until that interaction becomes optional conversation rather than handholding. To date this has never happened: no prompt has ever been issued to the agent through its own surface by the maintainer. That silence is the gap.

## Spec

1. **Interaction surface**: the live ember-cli window (the visible cockpit) — never a hidden headless bypass. Input via the focus-safe console mechanism; replies read from the same surface.
2. **Operator session receipts**: every session logs prompt/reply/next-action to receipts/operator-sessions/<UTC>.jsonl — the same process-visibility bar the repo enforces elsewhere. C-SURFACE2/C-OBS inherit these as live-provenance evidence.
3. **Goal injection first**: session 1 sets the agent's goal frame through its own surface (the equivalent of the goal-mode injection that governs the maintainer session) and responds to what returns.
4. **Cadence**: every work-loop window includes an operate-the-agent leg (prompt → observe → correct), mirroring the human→maintainer cadence one level down.
5. **Autonomy ladder coupling**: operator-session receipts become the R-rung evidence stream (issues #104/#109) — rungs claim when the agent needs FEWER operator interventions per window, measured from these receipts.
6. **Prerequisites prioritized because they gate this**: brain-server supervision (#122) and surface ports (#119).

## Acceptance

First operator-session receipt exists (prompt visibly issued in the cockpit, reply captured, next-action recorded); the operate-leg appears in the standing loop; ladder coupling documented in the R0 machinery.

title: ember-cli: flame animation jitters horizontally (per-frame width variance suspected) + art below bar
body:
Operator report (2026-07-04, live b16): "the fire/flame animation still looks like shit. not sure why it jitters left and right."

## Defect

The flame/fireball animation exhibits frame-to-frame HORIZONTAL displacement (left-right jitter) — the flame's visual center is not stationary across animation frames. Separately from the jitter, the overall art quality is below the operator bar even when stationary.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verify before fixing)

Most likely class: **per-frame width variance + per-frame centering**. If each ASCII/glyph frame has a different intrinsic width (trailing spaces trimmed, or art drawn with different margins per frame) and the renderer centers each frame on its OWN width, the centroid shifts every frame -> horizontal jitter. Same class if the frame strings mix wide glyphs/emoji with narrow chars so measured string width != rendered cell width on some frames (string-width vs terminal-cell mismatch).

Second candidate: Ink re-layout on content change — if the flame Box's measured width changes per frame, flex centering recomputes and shifts siblings too.

## Fix spec (frozen)

1. **Diagnose first, receipts:** dump each animation frame's raw string with per-line lengths + measured string-width; verify whether widths vary across frames. One JSON receipt with per-frame {frame_index, max_line_len, string_width} — the defect is proven when these numbers vary.

title: GPU window runbook: C11 flip -> E2B GATE-1/2 -> R3 phase B — frozen sequence + read-only pre-flight
body:
Frozen runbook spec for today's post-crossing GPU window. The window must convert the C11 24h crossing into up to three condition-bearing receipt sets without a mis-launch burning GPU hours; the launch knowledge currently lives as prose across #48, #47, and the paired protocol — this issue freezes it as ONE numbered, pre-flighted sequence. Maintainer executes every launch; the builder lane's job is the READ-ONLY pre-flight of each step against the live tree (the fixture-vs-live coverage rule: fixtures prove mechanisms, only the live target proves coverage).

## Sequence (strict order, one GPU job at a time)

**S0 — window entry gate.** C11 runner's own state shows cumulative >= 24h; runner is left RUNNING (it never pauses). Predicates: state JSON cumulative field >= 86400 (exact field name verified by pre-flight); `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` shows exactly one C11 runner. Abort criterion: crossing not reached → window does not open.

**S1 — C11 board flip.** Run the frozen C11 probe against the crossing receipts; verdict read from the receipt's verdict line in a SEPARATE call (probes exit 0 on RED). Flip-pair PENDING_AUTHORIZATION.json, board re-run, tally receipt. Predicates: probe verdict line == GREEN-equivalent; tally count increments by exactly 1.

**S2 — E2B GATE-1 (attach recon on the real weights).** Per protocol v1.1 clause 1's named prerequisite: LoRA attach at the E2B head linear + one zero-lr backward on the REAL local E2B module graph (9.6GB weights), non-mutating wrapper, gradient-isolation assert. Cheap, fail-fast, gates GATE-2. Predicates: attach succeeds; exactly the wrapper's params trainable; zero-lr step leaves param hash unchanged; VRAM margin assert per governor (fraction 0.8) before AND after load. Abort: any assert → window continues to S4 (R3), E2B escalates with the wall named.

**S3 — E2B GATE-2 (the one real training job).** `ember_c_e2b_paired_run.py --live` per #48: 1024-step iGRPO/LoRA at the E2B head, 16 checkpoint evals, wall ceiling 12768.6s, owned arm CITED from fire-4 via the cured loader (base-identity assert per protocol v1.3), founder_likeness 3-part session BOTH arms (300s continuation windows), provenance pin, api_spend 0. Launch requirements: PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, stdout unpiped to a receipt-adjacent log, tree-quiescence check first (`git -C B:/M/ember status --short scripts/` clean-or-owned — builder lanes have uncommitted GATE-0 edits there: pre-flight must enumerate them and confirm they are the RUN'S OWN files, not mid-edit foreign WIP), CPU builder lanes capped at 2 for the duration. Monitoring: alternation covering progress AND failure signatures (loss lines | Traceback | CUDA | OOM | assert), GPU util as liveness fallback, receipt path as completion signal. Verdict: from the assembly receipt's own falsifier fields, separate call.

**S4 — R3 phase B (only if S3 receipt landed or S2 aborted, AND the A2''' download verified).** `scripts/r3_feasibility_probe.py --model B:/M/models/Qwen3.6-27B` (no --dry-run): NF4 load, rank-64 slice attach, frozen-base grad assert, one train step + one inference pass co-resident, VRAM/nvidia-smi legs live, receipt to receipts/r3-feasibility/. Pre-registered branches: PASS / FAIL-VRAM / FAIL-DEPS — all three are valid publishable outcomes.

**S5 — window exit.** Process-visibility receipt refresh (landings occurred); board tally re-run if any flip; kill nothing — C11 runner and :8080 server survive the window.

## Builder pre-flight deliverable (read-only, no GPU, no CUDA calls, no launches)
For EACH step: (a) the exact command line(s) with every path/flag resolved against the live tree TODAY; (b) each predicate as a runnable read-only check with its expected output captured now (e.g. the C11 state field name + current value, the quiescence enumeration with each dirty file classified owned/foreign, current VRAM baseline via nvidia-smi, the A2''' download's current byte progress); (c) named gaps — anything the runbook references that does not resolve (missing file, wrong flag, ambiguous field) — the pre-flight's whole purpose is to find these while holding, not at 15:00Z. Receipt: one markdown report + a JSON of predicate checks under scratch/gpu-window-preflight/.

## Rails (verbatim-binding)
Builder lane: read-only everywhere (Read/Grep/Glob + read-only python probes); NEVER launches any step; NEVER touches ember_resident_igrpo.py / rig semantics; no CUDA context creation (nvidia-smi subprocess is allowed — it is a query tool, not a CUDA call); receipts under scratch/ only; kill-discipline N/A (nothing spawned); the maintainer executes S0-S5.

title: R3 feasibility receipt: 4-bit frozen 27B-class base + trainable slice, one train step + one inference pass co-resident on the 4090
body:
Compiled from docs/design/scale-architecture-frontier-20260703.md (action 2) — the regime table's conclusion: R3 (quantized-frozen majority + trained sparse slice) is the only regime satisfying "training AND inference, >27B total, on the 4090, not taking years." This issue is the first evidence leg: prove co-residence empirically, numbers not arithmetic.

## Deliverable

One receipt (`receipts/r3-feasibility/r3-feasibility-<ts>.json`) proving, in a SINGLE process on the 4090:
1. a ~27B-class base loaded 4-bit frozen (NF4/bitsandbytes-class, NOT a GGUF inference-only path — the slice must backprop),
2. a trainable LoRA-class slice attached (target ~100-300M trainable params, exact count recorded),
3. ONE verified training step on the slice (loss computed, backward, optimizer step; grad-norm > 0 recorded; frozen-base assert: zero base params with grad),
4. ONE inference pass (greedy, >=64 new tokens) WITHOUT unloading anything,
5. VRAM peak (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated + nvidia-smi sample) under the 0.80 governor fraction with the margin assert, tokens/s for both legs, wall-clock.

## Phase A — CPU prep (dispatchable NOW, no GPU touch; the duration keystone owns the GPU until its 24h crossing)

- A1 dependency probe: bitsandbytes + peft + transformers import cleanly on this Windows box; record versions. NO CUDA calls in phase A — import/metadata checks only.

If none exists in a trainable format, name the smallest suitable candidate + download size in the phase-A report; download only after maintainer ack (disk courtesy, resumable, sha-verified).
- A3 harness script (`scripts/r3_feasibility_probe.py`): all five receipt legs implemented behind asserts that FAIL CLOSED (governor fraction read from the standard config, margin assert before and after load, frozen-base grad assert, receipt written only if every assert passed). Deterministic, one-command, `--dry-run` mode that exercises everything but the CUDA calls.
- A4 pre-registered interpretation (frozen here): PASS = all five legs green under governor -> R3 regime EMPIRICALLY OPEN on this hardware (frontier doc's conclusion stands on a receipt). FAIL-VRAM = co-residence exceeds budget -> record the exact overshoot; the cure lane is slice-size/base-size sweep, not abandonment. FAIL-DEPS = kernel/library wall on Windows -> the wall gets named precisely (op, version, error) and broken (WSL2 fallback leg, source build, or kernel substitute) — never resolved to "unsupported."

## Phase B — GPU execution (maintainer-launched, post-crossing; ONE GPU job at a time)

Maintainer runs the harness in their own background with failure-signature monitoring; the builder never launches GPU work.

## Rails (verbatim-binding on any lane taking this)

- No edits outside scripts/ + receipts/r3-feasibility/ + a scratch subdir.

title: 8l contingency: mechanism-redesign ladder (adapter locus / objective / presentation) — fires only on A20 rung 2
body:
## Frozen contingency spec — 8l mechanism-redesign ladder (result-blind, pre-registered BEFORE A20's verdict)

**Why now, before A20 lands:** issue #36 rung 2 (A19's shape reproduced at 1.7× params) REFUTES the capacity hypothesis and BANS further C14 GPU windows until a mechanism-redesign spec "8l" is frozen. Writing 8l after seeing the result invites post-hoc rationalization; this spec is authored while A20 is mid-flight and blind to its outcome. **Execution precondition: A20 verdict = rung 2.** If A20 lands rung 1 (held-out ≥1/3 anywhere), this issue CLOSES UNEXECUTED with a comment recording that capacity was the binding constraint — that closure is itself evidence.

**Frame (from the A15–A19 synthesis + 0/16 seed invariance):** the protocol reliably builds a train-set lookup and never transfers. If 1.7× capacity doesn't move held-out, the remaining suspect class is the MECHANISM: where the adaptation lives (locus), what the objective rewards (outcome-only), and how the rule is presented (exemplar-conditioned). One arm per suspect, single variable each, all against the SAME substrate A20 used.

### Arm L1 — adapter locus (head-only → interior)
LoRA currently attaches ONLY at the head linear: the trained delta can at best re-map output logits of representations the frozen base already computes — a lookup-shaped inductive bias. L1 moves the same rank budget to interior FF projections (mid-depth layers, up+down proj), head untouched. CPU toy validation first (same TinyPolicyTransformer path as the seed study, 3 seeds); one GPU window only if the toy shape differs from head-only. Kill: toy held-out still 0/3 across all 3 seeds AND train acquisition unchanged → locus alone is not the lever.

### Arm L2 — objective (outcome reward → train-internal transfer pressure)
iGRPO rewards single-state outcomes; nothing prices generalization. L2 adds a train-internal transfer term: per batch, reward is granted only when the SAME adapter state answers correctly on a train state whose exemplar context omits that state (train states only — held-out remains untouched and unseen, the firewall is unchanged). Pre-registered risk: reward sparsity collapse; mitigation = anneal the transfer-term weight 0→λ over the first 256 steps. Kill: degenerate-resample trips >3× A19's rate OR train acquisition never reaches the seed-band floor (2/5 by step 320).

### Arm L3 — presentation (exemplar-conditioned → internalized)
k=3 exemplars in every training presentation mean the rule is always available in-context; the adapter can pass training without ever internalizing it. L3 anneals k 3→0 across training (schedule pre-registered at fire time from the corpus generator's existing knobs, no new mechanism). Eval unchanged (held-out protocol identical). Kill: train acquisition collapses to 0/5 at k=0 and never recovers by step 768.

### Discipline
- One arm per GPU window, order L1→L2→L3 (cheapest-inference-about-mechanism first); each arm's fire requires the previous arm's receipted verdict comment here.
- Same substrate as A20 (grown step-00000766, sha 58e8e989...), same envelope v2.2 otherwise, same seed-study interpretation bands, `EMBER_GATE_AUTHORIZED=1`, `EMBER_VRAM_FRACTION=0.80`, receipts to `receipts/ember-c14-owned-run/`.
- Held-out set is NEVER touched by any arm's training or reward computation — L2's transfer term reads train states only.
- No arm combines with another until one shows held-out >0 alone (no un-registered compositions).
- 3 arms exhausted with held-out still 0 → escalate to the operator with the full negative trail; the next hypothesis class (corpus/task structure) needs operator-level scope judgment.

# GOAL.md contract-integrity audit — 2026-07-03

Adversarial audit of the goal contract against on-disk reality: 102 binding mandates extracted

## Headline counts

- **13 internal defects** in GOAL.md (contradictions / stale-vs-disk text).
- **26 mandates fully UNWATCHED** + 64 partially watched (of 102): violation would not turn any
  board row RED.
- **7 operator-doc divergences** (2 crash-class, from 33 documented commands executed).

## Class 1 — contract text contradicts on-disk reality (stale-text cures, maintainer-landable)

| id | defect | cure |

title: C-OBS operator surface: monitor rendering overhaul, prompt, ANSI-safe wrap, ambient --watch observatory
body:
## Frozen spec: C-OBS operator surface — REPL rendering overhaul + ambient watch mode

### Defects found (operator-visible, all reproduced)

1. `monitor` dumped each board condition's FULL forensic verdict paragraph raw (some rows ~500 words) — no hierarchy, no color, no sort. Unusable as an observatory.
2. Header printed `pct_complete=0` beside 23 GREEN rows — field-read bug: adapter read `summary.pct_complete`, real value lives at `summary.completion_math.pct_complete`.
3. The REPL never called `rl.prompt()` — zero input cue after boot; surface looks hung.
4. Banner lines hard-wrapped mid-word at terminal width (`<of ferId>`, `proof-p ack`).
5. `commands/world-state.ts` (not-yet-live slash surface) duplicated defects 1-2.

### Contract (landed on the local workbench; lands here as a PR once seed branches merge)

- Pure renderer module `core/monitor-render.ts`: 2-line header (board ts, N/30 GREEN + true pct, incident count), one aligned line per condition `[idx] [G|R|A] NAME reason-first-sentence…` (sentence-aware truncate ≤110 chars), not-green rows sorted FIRST, ANSI color with NO_COLOR/non-TTY plain fallback; full forensics stay behind `evidence <surface> <n>`, index-consistent with the sorted view via one shared `sortMonitorConditions`.
- Prompt: `ember> ` (cyan/TTY, plain otherwise) after boot and after every command, never after `quit`.
- ANSI-safe word-boundary wrap routed through a single print choke point (escape codes never split, colors reset+reopen across breaks, multi-space column padding preserved).
- Compact 4-line banner; membrane/proof-pack prose relocated behind `understand` (verbatim, not deleted).
- `--watch [--interval N]` mode: non-interactive auto-refresh observatory — fresh state re-read per cycle, same board renderer, newest-3-receipts tail with ages, refresh-error resilience (never crashes the window), clean SIGINT exit.
- Both surfaces (REPL + slash command) consume the same renderer module.

### Acceptance criteria (all verified)

- Full ember-cli suite green with zero regressions; every contract item above carries dedicated unit tests (baseline 2340 pass → 2399 pass / 0 fail at item-5 completion; watch-mode tests additional on top).
- Piped end-to-end run against real contract-tree data: compact board with correct pct, prompt count = boot + 1/command, `evidence monitor 0` resolves the same row the sorted list displays.
- Subprocess-spawned E2E tests (the REPL calls `process.exit`; in-process module mocking corrupts the shared registry — spawned-fixture pattern is the mandated test shape for this surface).
